body.translated_text: Composed by <s>Śrī Jayadeva Gosvāmī</s>, the poem <s>Gīta Govinda</s>
<s>Śrī Gīta Govinda</s> Poem. (1) First Canto: <s>Sāmoda-Dāmodara</s> (The Joyful <s>Dāmodara</s>)

children.text: meghair meduraṃ ambaraṃ vana-bhuvaḥ śyāmās tamāla-drumair naktaṃ bhīrur ayaṃ tvam eva tad imaṃ rādhe gṛhaṃ prāpaya |
children.translated_text: The sky is thick with clouds, the forest grounds are dark with <s>tamāla</s> trees; this one is afraid in the night — you alone, O <s>Rādhā</s>, lead him home.

children.text: itthaṃ nanda-nideśataś calitayoḥ praty-adhva-kuñja-drumaṃ rādhā-mādhavayor jayanti yamunā-kūle rahaḥ-kelayaḥ || GG_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, as the two set out at <s>Nanda</s>'s command, the secret love-play of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s> on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, by the trees of the wayside bower, is triumphant. [GG 1.1]
He whose heart-temple is adorned with the deeds of the goddess of speech (<s>Vāgdevatā</s>), the sovereign who serves at the feet of <s>Padmāvatī</s>,

children.text: śrī-vāsudeva-rati-keli-kathā-sametaṃ etaṃ karoti jayadeva-kaviḥ prabandhaṃ || GG_1.2 ||
children.translated_text: this composition, replete with the tale of <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s>'s amorous play, the poet <s>Jayadeva</s> creates. [GG 1.2]

children.text: yadi hari-smaraṇe sarasaṃ mano yadi vilāsa-kalāsu kutūhalaṃ |
children.translated_text: If your mind delights in the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>, if you are curious about the arts of love-play,
then listen to this poetry of <s>Jayadeva</s>, with its sweet, tender, and lovely sequence of words. [GG 1.3]

body.text: vacaḥ pallavayaty umāpatidharaḥ sandarbha-śuddhiṃ girāṃ jānītejayadeva eva śaraṇaḥ ślāghyo durūha-druteḥ |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"durūhādbhuteḥ" (of profound wonder) is
an
alternate reading.}

children.text: śṛṅgārottara-sat-prameya-racanair ācārya-govardhana-spardhī ko'pi na viśrutaḥ srutidharo dhoyī kavi-kṣmāpatiḥ || GG_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: In amorous compositions of excellent themes, none is famed who rivals master <s>Govardhana</s>; <s>Dhoyī</s>, keeper of the scriptures, is a king among poets. [GG 1.4]

body.translated_text: The devotee of <s>Umāpati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) causes speech to blossom forth; <s>Jayadeva</s> alone is the refuge who knows purity of composition in verse, praiseworthy for his profound eloquence.
|| First composition ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Mālava-Gauḍa</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Rūpaka</s> <s>tāla</s>. <s>Aṣṭapadī</s> (eight-verse song)

body.text:
pralaya-payodhijale dhṛtavān asi vedaṃ vihita-vahitra-caritram akhedam |
keśava dhṛta-mīna-śarīra jaya jagadīśa hare [dhruva-padam] || GG_1.5 || (1.1)
body.translated_text: In the waters of the deluge, you upheld the <s>Veda</s>, performing the deeds of a boat without weariness. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the body of a fish, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [refrain] [GG 1.5] (1.1)

body.text:
kṣitir ativipulatare tava tiṣṭhati pṛṣṭhe dharaṇī-dharaṇa-kiṇa-cakra-gariṣṭhe |
keśava dhṛta-kacchapa-rūpa jaya jagadīśa hare || GG_1.6 || (1.2)
body.translated_text: The earth, exceedingly vast, rests upon your back, most weighty with the callous-rings of bearing the world. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the form of a tortoise, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.6] (1.2)

body.text:
vasati daśana-śikhare dharaṇī tava lagnā śaśini kalaṅka-kaleva nimagnā |
keśava dhṛta-sūkara-rūpa jaya jagadīśa hare || GG_1.7 || (1.3)
body.translated_text: The earth rests upon the tip of your tusk, clinging like the blemish upon the moon, as if submerged. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the form of a boar, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.7] (1.3)

body.text:
tava kara-kamala-vare nakhaṃ adbhuta-śṛṅgaṃ dalita-hiraṇyakaśipu-tanu-bhṛṅgaṃ |
keśava dhṛta-nara-hari-rūpa jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.8 || (1.4)
body.translated_text: On the excellent lotus of your hand, the nail is a wondrous horn, tearing apart the body of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> like a bee [tearing a flower]. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the form of the man-lion (<s>Narahari</s>), victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.8] (1.4)

body.text:
chalayasi vikramaṇe balim adbhuta-vāmana pada-nakha-nīra-janita-jana-pāvana |
keśava dhṛta-vāmana-rupa jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.9 || (1.5)
body.translated_text: You deceive <s>Bali</s> with [your] striding, O wondrous dwarf; the water born from [your] toenail purifies the people. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the form of the dwarf (<s>Vāmana</s>), victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.9] (1.5)

body.text:
kṣatrīya-rudhira-maye jagad apagata-pāpaṃ snapayasi payasi śamita-bhava-tāpam |
keśava dhṛta-bhṛgu-pati-rūpa jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.10 || (1.6)
body.translated_text: You bathe the world, freed from sin and drenched in the blood of the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, in waters that quench the fever of worldly existence. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the form of <s>Bhṛgupati</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.10] (1.6)

body.text:
vitarasi dikṣu raṇe dik-pati-kamanīyaṃ daśa-mukha-mauli-bali ramaṇīyam |
keśava dhṛta-rāma-śarīra jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.11 || (1.7)

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"raghupati-rūpam" (form of the Lord of the <s>Raghus</s>) is the reading of the Ha-edition.}

body.translated_text: You distribute in battle in all directions the lovely tribute of the heads of the ten-faced one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), delightful to the lords of the quarters. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the body of <s>Rāma</s>, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.11] (1.7)

body.text:
vahasi vapuṣi viśade vasanaṃ jaladābhaṃ hala-hati-bhīti-milita-yamunābham |
keśava dhṛta-hala-dhara-rūpa jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.12 || (1.8)
body.translated_text: You bear upon your radiant body a garment dark as a cloud, resembling the <s>Yamunā</s> darkened by fear of the plough's blow. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the form of the plough-bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>), victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.12] (1.8)

body.text:
nindasi yajña-vidher ahaha śruti-jātam sadaya-hṛdaya darśita-paśu-ghātam |
keśava dhṛta-buddha-śarīra jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.13 || (1.9)
body.translated_text: You condemn the ritual of sacrifice — alas! — born from scripture, revealing the slaughter of animals with a compassionate heart. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the body of the <s>Buddha</s>, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.13] (1.9)

body.text:
mleccha-nivaha-nidhane kalayasi karavālaṃ dhūma-ketum iva kim api karālam |
keśava dhṛta-kalki-śarīra jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.14 || (10)
body.translated_text: For the destruction of the hordes of barbarians (<s>mlecchas</s>), you wield the sword, terrifying like a blazing comet. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the body of <s>Kalki</s>, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.14] (1.10)

body.text:
śrī-jayadeva-kaver idam uditam udāraṃ śṛṇu sukhadaṃ śubhadaṃ bhava-sāram |
keśava dhṛta-daśa-vidha-rūpa jaya jagad-īśa hare || GG_1.15 || (11)
body.translated_text: This noble [song] is uttered by the poet <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> — listen! It is joy-giving, auspicious, the essence of worldly existence. O <s>Keśava</s>, who assumed the ten forms, victory to you, O Lord of the world, O <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.15] (1.11)

body.text:
vedān uddharate jaganti vahate bhūgolam udbibhrate daityaṃ dārayate baliṃ chalayate kṣatra-kṣayaṃ kurvate |
paulastyaṃ jayate halaṃ kalayate kāruṇyam ātanvate mlecchān mūrcchayate daśākṛti-kṛte kṛṣṇāya tubhyaṃ namaḥ || GG_1.16 || (5)
body.translated_text: You rescue the <s>Vedas</s>, bear the worlds, lift up the earth-globe, tear apart the demon, deceive <s>Bali</s>, bring about the destruction of the warrior class, conquer the descendant of <s>Pulastya</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>), wield the plough, extend compassion, lay low the barbarians — homage to you, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who wrought the ten forms! [GG 1.16] (5)
|| Composition 2 ||

children.translated_text: In <s>Gurjarī</s> <s>rāga</s>, <s>Niḥsāra</s>
<s>tāla</s>,
it is sung

body.text:
śrita-kamalā-kuca-maṇḍala dhṛta-kuṇḍala e
kalita-lalita-vana-māla
jaya jaya deva hare || GG_1.17 ||[dhruva-padam]
body.translated_text: O you who rest upon the bosom of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), wearing earrings, adorned with a lovely forest garland — victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.17] [refrain]

children.translated_text: destroyer of worldly existence,
O swan dwelling in the minds of sages —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.18]

body.translated_text: O ornament of the orb of the sun-jewel,

children.translated_text: delighter of people,
O sun of the lotus [pond] of the <s>Yadu</s> clan —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.19]

body.translated_text: O vanquisher of the poison-bearing serpent <s>Kāliya</s>,

children.translated_text: O destroyer of <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Mura</s>, and <s>Naraka</s>,
seated upon <s>Garuḍa</s>,
O cause of the sport of the gods —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.20]
liberator from worldly existence,
O treasure-house of the three worlds —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.21]

body.translated_text: O you whose eyes are like spotless lotus petals,

children.translated_text: conqueror of <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>,
who pacified the ten-necked one (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>) in battle —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.22]

body.translated_text: O you adorned by the daughter of <s>Janaka</s> (<s>Sītā</s>),

children.translated_text: bearer of Mount <s>Mandara</s>,
O <s>cakora</s> bird to the moon of <s>Śrī</s>'s face —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.23]

body.translated_text: O you who are beautiful like a fresh rain cloud,

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"caraṇe" (at the foot)}
so consider, O Lord —
grant welfare to those who bow before you —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.24]

body.translated_text: We bow at your feet —

children.translated_text: brings delight —
a radiant, auspicious song —
victory, victory to <s>Deva</s> <s>Hari</s>! [GG 1.25]

body.translated_text: This [song] by the poet <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>

children.translated_text: The chest of <s>Madhusūdana</s>, stamped with saffron from the embrace of the slopes of <s>Padmā</s>'s (<s>Lakṣmī</s>'s) breasts,

children.text: vyaktānurāgam iva khelad-anaṅga-kheda-svedāmbu-pūram anupūrayatu priyaṃ vaḥ || GG_1.26 ||
children.translated_text: as if displaying open love with a flood of perspiration born of the weariness of playful <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Love-god) — may it fulfill your desires! [GG 1.26]

children.text: vasante vāsantī-kusuma-sukumārair avayavair bhramantīṃ kāntāre bahu-vihita-kṛṣṇānusaraṇām |
children.translated_text: In spring, as [<s>Rādhā</s>] wandered in the forest with limbs tender as spring flowers, having long pursued <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: amandaṃ kandarpa-jvara-janita-cintākulatayā valad-bādhāṃ rādhāṃ sarasam idam ūce sahacarī || GG_1.27 ||
children.translated_text: greatly afflicted by the anxiety born of the fever of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the Love-god), her companion spoke these heartfelt words to the distressed <s>Rādhā</s>: [GG 1.27]
NOTE:
{"calad" (trembling) is
an
alternate reading.}

body.translated_text: || Composition 3 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Vasanta</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Yati</s> <s>tāla</s>
In the gentle <s>Malaya</s> breeze, soft from caressing the lovely clove-vine (<s>lavaṅga-latā</s>),
in the bower-cottage resounding with the cooing of cuckoos mingled with swarms of bees — [GG 1.28]

body.text:
viharati harir iha sarasa-vasante
nṛtyati yuvatī-janena samaṃ sakhi virahi-janasya durante ||dhr||
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here in the delightful spring, dancing with the young women together — O friend, [a time] unbearable for those separated [from their lovers]! [refrain]

children.translated_text: In [the season] that arouses the laments of the wives of travellers maddened by the desires of <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god),
in the groves of <s>bakula</s> trees filled undisturbed with clusters of flowers thronged by swarms of bees — [GG 1.29]
In the <s>tamāla</s> trees with fresh garlands of leaves, obedient to the rushing fragrance of musk,
in the network of <s>kiṃśuka</s> flowers, gleaming like the nails of the Love-god that tear apart the hearts of the young — [GG 1.30]
In the blooming <s>keśara</s> flowers, lovely as the golden staff of <s>Madana</s>, king of the earth,
in the sport of the rows of bees gathered on the pinkish petals, making as if quivers for the Love-god — [GG 1.31]
In [the season] that smiles tenderly and compassionately, gazing upon the world that has shed its modesty,
where the <s>ketaka</s> flower, with its spear-point shape, cuts asunder the hopes of those separated [from their lovers] — [GG 1.32]
NOTE:
{"mālikayātisugandhau" is
an

children.text:
pāṭhāntaraḥ.}
muni-manasām api mohana-kārīṇi taruṇa||-karaṇa-bandhau || GG_1.33 ||
children.translated_text:
alternate reading.}
Captivating even the minds of sages, in the bonds of the youthful season — [GG 1.33]

body.translated_text: Delightful with the fragrance of the <s>mādhavikā</s> creeper, sweet-scented with fresh <s>mālatī</s> and <s>jāti</s> flowers,

children.translated_text: In the <s>cūta</s> (mango) trees, with buds bristling with delight from the embrace of the blooming <s>atimukta</s> creepers around them,
in the environs of the grove of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, purified by the nearby waters of the <s>Yamunā</s> — [GG 1.34]
Thus spoken by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>, this [song] arises, its essence being the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s feet,
a description of the forest in the delightful spring season, pervaded by the agitation of desire. [GG 1.35]
With the wafting pollen from the gently opening jasmine (<s>mallī</s>) vines, perfuming the forests with the fragrance of garments,

children.text: iha hi dahati cetaḥ ketakī-gandha-bandhuḥ prasarad-asama-bāṇa-prāṇavad gandhavāhaḥ || GG_1.36 ||
children.translated_text: here indeed the wind, companion of the <s>ketakī</s> fragrance, burns the heart, like the breath of the unequal-arrowed one (<s>Kāma</s>) himself. [GG 1.36]
NOTE:

{In the edition with <s>Haridāsa Dāsa</s>'s <s>Prabodhānanda</s> commentary, verse number 48 is found.}
Afflicted with fever in the ear by the playful cries and cooing of cuckoos sporting on mango buds shaking with the bees greedy for the scent of bursting honey,
NOTE:
{"kala-ravair" (with sweet sounds) is
an
alternate reading.}

children.text: nīyante pathikaiḥ kathaṃ katham api dhyānāvadhāna-kṣaṇa prāpta-prāṇa-samāgama-rasollāsair amī vāsarāḥ || GG_1.37 ||
children.translated_text: these days are somehow passed by travelers through moments of meditation, with the joy of attaining union with the life-breath. [GG 1.37]
Displaying <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who is eager for charming play, gleaming with the excitement of embracing many women, from nearby,

children.text: murārim ārād upadarśayanty asau sakhī samakṣaṃ punar āha rādhikām || GG_1.38 ||
children.translated_text: that companion again spoke to <s>Rādhikā</s> before [her] eyes: [GG 1.38]

body.translated_text: || Composition 4 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Rāmakarī</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Yati</s> <s>tāla</s>
With body anointed with sandal paste, dark-complexioned, wearing yellow garments and a forest garland,
adorned with jeweled earrings swaying in play, his cheeks graced with a smile — [GG 1.39]

body.text: harir iha mugdha-vadhū-nikare vilāsini vilāsati kelī-pare ||dhr||
body.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports here amidst the group of charming young women, O beautiful one, devoted to amorous play! [refrain]

children.translated_text: Embracing <s>Hari</s> passionately under the weight of her full breasts,
a certain cowherd-woman sings along, her voice rising in the fifth mode (<s>pañcama rāga</s>). [GG 1.40]
A certain one, with amorous, playfully rolling glances that arouse desire —
the charming young woman meditates deeply upon the lotus-face of <s>Madhusūdana</s>. [GG 1.41]

children.text: kāpi kapola-tale militā lapituṃ kim api śruti-mūle |
children.translated_text: A certain one, her cheek pressed close, whispers something in his ear;

children.text: cāru cucumba nitambavatī dayitaṃ pulakair anukūle || GG_1.42 ||
children.translated_text: the full-hipped beauty charmingly kissed her beloved, [his body covered] with goosebumps of delight. [GG 1.42]
With eager curiosity for the arts of love-play, a certain one, at the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
dragged by [his] garment with her hand [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], who had entered the lovely bower of <s>vañjula</s> trees. [GG 1.43]
With the sweet sound of bangles tinkling on hands keeping the beat, blending with the flute,

children.text: rāsa-rase saha-nṛtya-parā hariṇā yuvatī praśaśaṃse || GG_1.44 ||
children.translated_text: a young woman, devoted to dancing with <s>Hari</s> in the delight of the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, was praised. [GG 1.44]

children.text: śliṣyati kām api cumbati kām api kām api ramayati rāmām |
children.translated_text: He embraces one, kisses another, and pleasures yet another beautiful woman;

children.text: paśyati sa smita-cāru-tarām aparām anugacchati vāmām || GG_1.45 ||
children.translated_text: he gazes at another with a charming smile, and follows yet another coy one. [GG 1.45]
This wondrous secret of <s>Keśava</s>'s love-play, as spoken by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>,

children.text: vṛndāvana-vipine lalitaṃ vitanotu śubhāni yaśasyam || GG_1.46 ||
children.translated_text: a graceful [song set] in the grove of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — may it bestow auspiciousness and fame! [GG 1.46]
NOTE:
{"valitam" (graceful) is also a reading.}

children.text: viśveṣām anurañjanena janayann ānandam indīvara-śreṇī-śyāmala-komalair upanayann aṅgair anaṅgotsavam |
children.translated_text: Delighting all beings with his charm, bringing on a festival of love with limbs soft and dark as a row of blue lotuses,

children.text: svacchandaṃ vraja-sundarībhir abhitaḥ praty-aṅgam āliṅgitaḥ śṛṅgāraḥ sakhi mūrtimān iva madhau mugdho hariḥ krīḍati || GG_1.47 ||
children.translated_text: freely embraced limb by limb on all sides by the beauties of <s>Vraja</s> — O friend, <s>Hari</s>, love incarnate, plays enchanted in the spring! [GG 1.47]
NOTE:
{"adryotsaṅga-" or "adyotsaṅga-" is
an
alternate reading.}

children.text: kiṃ ca snigdha-rasāla-mauli-mukulāny ālokya harṣodayād unmīlanti kuhūḥ kuhūr iti kalottālāḥ pikānāṃ giraḥ || GG_1.48 ||
children.translated_text: and moreover, seeing the buds on the tops of the tender mango trees, the melodious voices of the cuckoos burst forth in rapturous cries of "kuhū, kuhū!" [GG 1.48]

body.translated_text: As if fleeing the torment of the serpent dwelling on his own peak, the <s>Malaya</s> mountain breeze pursues Mount <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (Sandal Mountain), wishing to swim in the snow,

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{This verse is not read by <s>Prabodhānanda</s>.}

children.text: rāsollāsa-bhareṇa vibhrama-bhṛtām ābhīra-vāma-bhruvām abhyarṇaṃ parirabhya nirbharam uraḥ premāndhayā rādhayā |
children.translated_text: Having embraced closely to his chest the coquettish <s>Ābhīra</s> women of lovely brows, intoxicated with the joy of the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, by love-blinded <s>Rādhā</s> —

children.text: sādhu tvad-vadanaṃ sudhā-mayam iti vyāhṛtya gīta-stuti-vyājād udbhaṭa-cumbitaḥ smita-manohāri hariḥ pātu vaḥ || GG_1.49 ||
children.translated_text: having declared "Your face is truly nectar-filled," and under the pretext of singing praise, kissed ardently — may <s>Hari</s>, smiling charmingly, protect you! [GG 1.49]
NOTE:
{"smṛta" (?)}

body.text: || iti śrī-gīta-govinde sāmoda-dāmodaro nāma prathamaḥ sargaḥ ||
body.translated_text: || Thus ends the first canto named <s>Sāmoda-Dāmodara</s> in the <s>Śrī Gīta Govinda</s>. ||
Second Canto: <s>Akleśa-Keśava</s> (The Untroubled <s>Keśava</s>)

children.text: viharati vane rādhā sādhāraṇa-praṇaye harau vigalita-nijotkarṣād īrṣyā-vaśena gatā'nyataḥ |
children.translated_text: While <s>Hari</s> sported in the forest with love shared among many, <s>Rādhā</s>, fallen from her own preeminence, went elsewhere, overcome by jealousy.

children.text: kvacid api latā-kuñje guñjan-madhu-vrata-maṇḍalī mukhara-śikhare līna dīnāpy uvāca rahaḥ sakhīm || GG_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Somewhere, hidden in a vine-bower on a peak buzzing with swarms of humming bees, she, distressed, spoke in secret to her companion: [GG 2.1]

body.translated_text: || Composition 5 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Gurjarī</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Yati</s> <s>tāla</s>

body.text:
sañcarad-adhara-sudhā-madhura-dhvani-mukharita-mohana-vaṃśam |
calita-dṛg-añcala-cañcala-mauli-kapola-vilola-vataṃsam |
rāse harim iha vihita-vilāsaṃ smarati mano mama kṛta-parihāsam || dhru. || GG_2.2 ||
body.translated_text: Playing the enchanting flute, sweetened by the nectar of his moving lips, with the hem of his tilting crown swaying over his cheeks, adorned with dancing, glancing eyes — my mind remembers <s>Hari</s>, engaged here in amorous play during the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, making sport [of me]. [refrain] [GG 2.2]

children.translated_text: With hair encircled by a lovely crest of peacock tail-feathers,
beautifully attired like a dense rain cloud tinged with the many-colored rainbow of <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) — [GG 2.3]
Whose desire was aroused by kissing the faces of the full-hipped cowherd women,
whose lips, tender as petals of the <s>bandhujīva</s> flower, blossomed with a radiant smile — [GG 2.4]
Embracing with his broad arms, sprouting with goosebumps, a thousand young cowherd women,
the darkness shattered by the rays of the jeweled ornaments on his hands, feet, and chest — [GG 2.5]
With a <s>tilaka</s> of sandal paste on his forehead, mocking the moon playing among the clouds,
Whose heart's door is merciless in pressing against the expanse of full breasts. || GG_2.6 ||
With cheeks adorned by charming jeweled <s>Makara</s>-shaped earrings, magnificent,
Wearing yellow garments, attended by an excellent retinue of sages, humans, gods, and demons. || GG_2.7 ||
Met beneath a bright <s>Kadamba</s> tree, quelling the fear of the impurity of the <s>Kali</s> age,

children.text: mām api kim api tarala-taraṅgad-anaṅga-dṛśā manasā ramayantam || GG_2.8 ||
children.translated_text: Delighting even me somehow with a gaze trembling with waves of desire, in the mind. || GG_2.8 ||
Spoken by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>, [this describes] the exceedingly beautiful, enchanting form of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>;

children.text: hari-caraṇa-smaraṇaṃ prati samprati puṇyavatām anurūpam || GG_2.9 ||
children.translated_text: For the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s feet, now fitting for the meritorious. || GG_2.9 ||

body.text: gaṇayati guṇa-grāmaṃ bhāmaṃ bhrāmād api nehate vahati ca paritoṣaṃ doṣaṃ vimuñcati dūrataḥ |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{Variant reading: bhrāmam}

children.text: yuvatiṣu valat-tṛṣṇe kṛṣṇe vihāriṇi māṃ vinā punar api mano vāmaṃ kāmaṃ karoti karomi kim || GG_2.10 ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with longing springing up, sports among young women without me, again my perverse mind desires [him] — what shall I do? || GG_2.10 ||

body.translated_text: He counts the multitude of virtues, does not heed even wrath through confusion, bears satisfaction, and casts off fault far away;
|| Song 6 ||

children.translated_text: [This is] sung in <s>Mālava-Gauḍa</s> <s>rāga</s> and <s>Ekatālī</s> <s>tāla</s>.

children.text: nibhṛta-nikuñja-gṛhaṃ gatayā niśi rahasi nilīya vasantam |
children.translated_text: To her who has gone to the secluded bower-house, having hidden there secretly at night, dwelling,
Looking startled in all directions, laughing with the fullness of love's fervor — || GG_2.11 ||

body.text:
sakhi he keśī-mathanam udāram
ramaya mayā saha madana-manoratha-bhāvitayā sa-vikāram ||dhruvam ||
body.translated_text: O friend, unite the noble slayer of <s>Keśī</s> with me, who am filled with love's desires, passionately. || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: With her shy at the first union, [him] favorable with hundreds of clever flatteries,
With her speaking with soft, sweet smiles, [him] whose hip-garment is loosened — || GG_2.12 ||
With her placed upon a bed of tender shoots, [him] lying upon my breast for a long time,
With her having made embraces and kisses, [him] having embraced and drunk from [her] lips — || GG_2.13 ||
With her having languidly half-closed eyes, [him] with cheeks beautified by rows of goosebumps,
With her whole body covered with the sweat of exertion, [him] exceedingly restless with the intoxication of excellent love — || GG_2.14 ||
With her cooing in the sweet tones of a cuckoo, [him] having conquered the strategies of the god of love,
With her having loosened locks filled with flowers, [him] whose full breast-mass is scratched by nails — || GG_2.15 ||
With her feet jingling with jeweled anklets, filling the canopy of love-play,
With her tinkling, loosened girdle, [him] giving kisses while grasping [her] hair — || GG_2.16 ||
With her languid with the essence of love's pleasure at its peak, [him] with lotus-eyes slightly closed,
With her, a slender vine fallen helplessly — [unite her with] <s>Madhusūdana</s>, whose desire has arisen. || GG_2.17 ||
This, spoken by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>, [describes] the surpassing love-play nature of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>;
May this account, told by the yearning cowherd wife, gracefully spread happiness. || GG_2.18 ||

[Him] with the playful flute slipping from his hand, with glances from the corners of his eyes scattering the group of cowherd women whose eyebrow-creepers are curved, with cheeks moist with excessive perspiration —

children.text: mām udvīkṣya vilajjitaṃ smṛta-sudhā-mugdhānana-kānane govindaṃ vraja-sundarī-gaṇa-vṛtaṃ paśyāmi hṛṣyāmi ca || GG_2.19 ||
children.translated_text: Looking up at me, embarrassed, remembering the nectar-sweet enchantment of [her] face — I see <s>Govinda</s> surrounded by the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>, and I rejoice. || GG_2.19 ||
The blossoming of new <s>Aśoka</s> creepers with barely visible clusters of flower-buds causes distress; even the breeze of the garden grove torments [her];

children.text: api bhrāmyad-bhṛṅgī-raṇita-ramaṇīyā na mukula-prasūtiś cūtānāṃ sakhi śikhariṇīyaṃ sukhayati || GG_2.20 ||
children.translated_text: Even the budding of mango trees, lovely with the sound of wandering bees — O friend, does not bring comfort. || GG_2.20 ||
With suggestive smiles, with hair-braids loosening in agitation, with eyebrow-creepers raised, with breasts half-revealed by a feigned hand-gesture at the shoulder —

children.text: gopīnāṃ nibhṛtaṃ nirīkṣya gamitākāṅkṣaś ciraṃ cintayann antar mugdha-manoharaṃ haratu vaḥ kleśaṃ navaḥ keśavaḥ || GG_2.21 ||
children.translated_text: Having secretly observed the <s>Gopīs</s> [thus], his longing aroused, pondering for a long time — may the youthful <s>Keśava</s>, inwardly enchanting and charming, remove your afflictions. || GG_2.21 ||

body.text:
iti śrī-gīta-govinda-mahā-kāvye akleśa-keśavo nāma
dvitīyaḥ sargaḥ
||2||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second canto named '<s>Akleśa-Keśava</s>' (The Effortless <s>Keśava</s>) in the great poem <s>Gīta Govinda</s>. ||2||
(3) Third Canto: <s>Mugdha-Madhusūdana</s> (The Bewildered Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>)

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{The reading vāsanābaddha- is from the <s>Caitanya Caritāmṛta</s>.}

children.text: rādhām ādhāya hṛdaye tatyāja vraja-sundarīḥ || GG_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Placing <s>Rādhā</s> in his heart, abandoned the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>. || GG_3.1 ||

body.translated_text: Even the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, [caught in] the chain bound by worldly desire —

children.text: itas tatas tām anusṛtya rādhikām anaṅga-bāṇa-vraṇa-khinna-mānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: Searching here and there for that <s>Rādhikā</s>, his mind afflicted by the wounds of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (the bodiless god of love's) arrows,

children.text: kṛtānutāpaḥ sa kalinda-nandinī-taṭānta-kuñje viṣasāda mādhavaḥ || GG_3.2 ||
children.translated_text: Full of remorse, that <s>Mādhava</s> sat despondent in a bower at the edge of the bank of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>). || GG_3.2 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 7 ||

children.translated_text: [This is] sung in <s>Gurjarī</s> <s>rāga</s> and <s>Yati</s> <s>tāla</s>.

children.text: mām iyaṃ calitā vilokya vṛtaṃ vadhū-nicayena |
children.translated_text: She departed, seeing me surrounded by a group of women;
Out of guilt, I too did not stop her, out of excessive fear. || GG_3.3 ||

body.text: hari hari hatādaratayā gatā sā kupiteva ||dhruva-padam ||
body.translated_text: Alas, alas! Through [my] lack of regard, she has gone away, as if angered. || Refrain ||

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyati kiṃ vadiṣyati sā ciraṃ viraheṇa |
children.translated_text: What will she do, what will she say, in long separation?

children.text: kiṃ dhanena janena kiṃ mama jīvitena gṛheṇa || GG_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: What use to me is wealth, people, my life, or home? || GG_3.4 ||
I think of that face, with eyebrows curved with the fullness of anger,
Like a red lotus troubled by a bee hovering above. || GG_3.5 ||

children.text: tām ahaṃ hṛdi saṅgatām aniśaṃ bhṛśaṃ ramayāmi |
children.translated_text: I delight in her intensely, united with her always in my heart;

children.text: kiṃ vane'nusarāmi tām iha kiṃ vṛthā vilapāmi || GG_3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Why do I follow her in the forest? Why do I lament here in vain? || GG_3.6 ||
O slender one, I perceive your heart is troubled by jealousy;

children.text: tan na vedmi kuto gatāsi na tena te'nunayāmi || GG_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: But I know not where you have gone, and therefore cannot appease you. || GG_3.7 ||

children.text: dṛśyase purato gatāgatam eva me vidadhāsi |
children.translated_text: You appear before me, you cause me only comings and goings;

children.text: kiṃ pureva sasambhramaṃ parirambhaṇaṃ na dadāsi || GG_3.8 ||
children.translated_text: Why do you not give me an eager embrace as before? || GG_3.8 ||

children.text: kṣamyatām aparaṃ kadāpi tavedṛśaṃ na karomi |
children.translated_text: Forgive me! Never again will I do such [a thing] to you;

children.text: dehi sundari darśanaṃ mama manmathena dunomi || GG_3.9 ||
children.translated_text: Grant me your sight, O beautiful one — I am tormented by <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love). || GG_3.9 ||
NOTE:
{Variant reading: pravaṇena (devout)}
The beloved of <s>Padmāvatī</s>, born in <s>Kindubilva</s> by the ocean. || GG_3.10 ||

body.translated_text: This [song] of <s>Hari</s> has been described by <s>Jayadeva</s>, who is devoted,

children.text: hṛdi bisa-latā-hāro nāyaṃ bhujaṅgama-nāyakaḥ kuvalaya-dala-śreṇī kaṇṭhe na sā garala-dyutiḥ |
children.translated_text: This lotus-fiber necklace on [my] heart is not the lord of serpents; this row of blue-lotus petals on [my] throat is not the gleam of poison;

children.text: malayaja-rajo nedaṃ bhasma priyā-rahite mayi prahara na hara-bhrāntyā'naṅga krudhā kim u dhāvasi || GG_3.11 ||
children.translated_text: This sandalwood dust is not ash — on me, bereft of my beloved, do not strike, O <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless god of love), mistaking [me] for <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>)! Why do you rush in anger? || GG_3.11 ||

children.text: pāṇau mā kuru cūta-sāyakam amuṃ mā cāpam āropaya kṛīḍā-nirjita-viśva mūrcchita-janāghātena kiṃ pauruṣam |
children.translated_text: Do not place that mango-blossom arrow in [your] hand, do not string [your] bow — O conqueror of the world in play, what heroism is there in striking one who has fainted?

children.text: tasyā eva mṛgī-dṛśo manasija preṇkhat-katākṣāśuga-śreṇī-jarjaritaṃ manāg api mano nādyāpi sandhukṣate || GG_3.12 ||
children.translated_text: O god of love, my mind, shattered by the shower of darting sidelong glances from that deer-eyed one alone, is not even slightly revived even now. || GG_3.12 ||

children.text: bhrū-pallavaṃ dhanur apāṅga-taraṇgitāni bāṇā guṇaḥ śravaṇa-pālir iti smareṇa |
children.translated_text: Her eyebrow-sprouts are the bow, her wavering sidelong glances are the arrows, her ear-edge is the bowstring — thus by <s>Smara</s> (the god of love),

children.text: tasyām anaṅga-jaya-jaṅgama-devatāyām astrāṇi nirjita-jaganti kim arpitāni || GG_3.13 ||
children.translated_text: In that mobile deity of love's conquest, have the world-conquering weapons been placed? || GG_3.13 ||

children.text: bhrū-cāpe nihitaḥ kaṭākṣa-viśikho nirmātu marma-vyathāṃ śyāmātmā kuṭilaḥ karotu kabarī-bhāro'pi mārodyamam |
children.translated_text: Let the arrow of the sidelong glance placed on the bow of her eyebrow produce anguish in the vitals; let even the mass of her dark, curling tresses make efforts for <s>Māra</s>'s (love's) destruction;

children.text: mohaṃ tāvad ayaṃ ca tanvi tanutāṃ bimba-dharo rāgavān sad-vṛttaḥ stana-maṇḍalas tava kathaṃ prāṇair mama krīḍati || GG_3.14 ||
children.translated_text: Let this passionate <s>Bimba</s>-fruit lip, O slender one, spread delusion — but how does the well-rounded orb of your breast play with my very life? || GG_3.14 ||

children.text: tāni sparśa-sukhāni te ca taralāḥ snigdhā dṛśor vibhramās tad-vaktrāmbuja-saurabhaṃ sa ca sudhā-syandi girāṃ vakrimā |
children.translated_text: Those pleasures of touch, and those trembling, tender playful glances; that fragrance of the lotus-face, and that nectar-dripping crookedness of speech;

children.text: sa bimbādhara-mādhurīti viṣayāsaṅge'pi cen mānasaṃ tasyāṃ lagna-samādhi hanta viraha-vyādhiḥ kathaṃ vardhate || GG_3.15 ||
children.translated_text: That sweetness of the <s>Bimba</s>-fruit lip — even when detached from sense objects, if the mind is fixed in deep absorption on her, alas, how does the disease of separation grow? || GG_3.15 ||
NOTE:
{The variant reading is
dīpti
(radiance).}

children.text: saṃmugdhe madhusūdanasya madhure rādhā-mukhendau sudhā-sāre kandalitāś ciraṃ dadatu vaḥ kṣemaṃ kaṭākṣormayaḥ || GG_3.16 ||
children.translated_text: In the enchanting, sweet moon-face of <s>Rādhā</s> before the bewildered <s>Madhusūdana</s>, full of nectar-essence — may the waves of sidelong glances that have arisen long grant you well-being. || GG_3.16 ||

body.translated_text: Of him whose diadem trembles as his crest sways with his neck turned sideways, not noticed by the marks of women attentive to the musical notes rising from his flute —

body.text:
iti śrī-gīta-govinda-mahā-kāvye mugdha-madhusūdano nāma
tṛtīyaḥ sargaḥ
||3||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third canto named '<s>Mugdha-Madhusūdana</s>' (The Bewildered Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>) in the great poem <s>Gīta Govinda</s>. ||3||
Fourth Canto: <s>Snigdha-Madhusūdana</s> (The Tender Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>)

children.translated_text: Seated gently in a bower of cane on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
<s>Rādhikā</s>'s friend spoke to <s>Mādhava</s>, distraught with the weight of love. || GG_4.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 8 ||

children.translated_text: [This is] sung in <s>Karṇāṭa</s> <s>rāga</s> and <s>Ekatālī</s> <s>tāla</s>.

children.text: nindati candanam indu-kiraṇam anu vindati khedam adhīram |
children.translated_text: She condemns the sandalwood [paste], she finds restless grief following the moonbeams;

children.text: vyāla-nilaya-milanena garalam iva kalayati malaya-samīram || GG_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: She considers the <s>Malaya</s> breeze as poison, as if encountering a serpent's abode. || GG_4.2 ||

children.text: mādhava manasija-viśikha-bhayād iva bhāvanayā tvayi līnā |
children.translated_text: O <s>Mādhava</s>, as if out of fear of <s>Kāma</s>'s (the god of love's) arrows, she is absorbed in you through meditation;
She is wretched in separation from you. || Refrain ||
As if for protection from the incessantly falling arrows of <s>Kāma</s>, wide,
She makes an armor of moist lotus-leaf clusters over the vital point of her heart. || GG_4.3 ||
On a bed of flower-arrows, beautiful with manifold arts of grace,

children.text: vratam iva tava parirambha-sukhāya karoti kusuma-śayanīyam || GG_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: As if a vow, she prepares a bed of flowers for the joy of your embrace. || GG_4.4 ||
She bears a stream of tears flowing from her stirring eyes on her noble lotus-face,
Like the moon [streaming] with the nectar flowing from the splitting fangs of the fierce <s>Rāhu</s>. || GG_4.5 ||
In private she draws you with musk, [depicting you] as the one who has become [<s>Kāma</s> with his] unequaled arrows;

children.text: praṇamati makaram adho vinidhāya kare ca śaraṃ nava-cūtam || GG_4.6 ||
children.translated_text: She bows down, having placed the <s>Makara</s> [emblem] below and in [your] hand a new mango-blossom arrow. || GG_4.6 ||

children.text: dhyāna-layena puraḥ parikalpya bhavantam atīva durāpam |
children.translated_text: Having imagined you before her through absorption in meditation, though you are so difficult to attain,

children.text: vilapati hasati viṣīdati roditi cañcati muñcati tāpam || GG_4.7 ||
children.translated_text: She laments, laughs, despairs, weeps, moves restlessly, and releases [her] anguish. || GG_4.7 ||

children.text: prati-padam idam api nigadati mādhava tava caraṇe patitāham |
children.translated_text: At every step she also says this: 'O <s>Mādhava</s>, I have fallen at your feet;'

children.text: tvayi vimukhe mayi sapadi sudhā-nidhir api tanute tanu-dāham || GG_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'When you are turned away from me, even the moon (treasury of nectar) immediately produces a burning in my body.' || GG_4.8 ||

children.text: śrī-jayadeva-bhaṇitam idam adhikaṃ yadi manasā naṭaṇīyam |
children.translated_text: If this, spoken by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>, is to be further danced upon in the mind,
Then the words of the friend of the cowherd maiden, distraught from separation from <s>Hari</s>, should be recited. || GG_4.9 ||

children.text: āvāso vipināyate priya-sakhī-mālāpi jālāyate tāpo'pi śvasitena dāva-dahana-jvāla-kalāpāyate |
children.translated_text: The dwelling has become a forest, the garland of dear friends has become a net; even the heat, through her sighing, has become a mass of forest-fire flames;

children.text: sāpi tvad-viraheṇa hanta hariṇī-rūpāyate hā kathaṃ kandarpo'pi yamāyate viracayan śārdūla-vikrīḍitam || GG_4.10 ||
children.translated_text: She too, alas, through separation from you, has taken the form of a doe — oh, how even <s>Kāma</s> has become like <s>Yama</s> (Death), composing [this] in <s>Śārdūlavikrīḍita</s> [meter]. || GG_4.10 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 9 ||

children.translated_text: [This is] sung in <s>Deśākhya</s> <s>rāga</s> and <s>Ekatālī</s> <s>tāla</s>.
Even the magnificent necklace placed upon her breasts —

children.text: sa manute kṛśā-tanur iva bhāram || GG_4.11 ||
children.translated_text: She considers a burden, as if her body were emaciated. || GG_4.11 ||

body.translated_text: O <s>Keśava</s>, <s>Rādhikā</s> in separation from you — || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: Even the moist, smooth sandalwood paste —

children.text: paśyati viṣam iva vapuṣi sa-śaṅkam || GG_4.12 ||
children.translated_text: She views with suspicion as poison on her body. || GG_4.12 ||
The wind of her sighing, of incomparable extent,
She bears like the fire of <s>Kāma</s>, with burning. || GG_4.13 ||
In every direction she scatters a net of tear-drops,
Like a lotus whose stalk has broken, [tears flowing] from her eyes. || GG_4.14 ||
She does not abandon [the resting of] her cheek on her palm,
Like the motionless young moon at evening. || GG_4.15 ||
Even the bed of tender sprouts before her eyes —
She considers to be an arrangement of fire. || GG_4.16 ||

children.text: harir iti harir iti japati sa-kāmam |
children.translated_text: She chants '<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>' with longing,
As if death ordained by separation, exceedingly. || GG_4.17 ||
This song, thus spoken by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>,
May it bring happiness, having led [one] to the state of <s>Keśava</s>. || GG_4.18 ||

children.text: sā romāñcati śītkaroti vilapaty utkampate tāmyati dhyāyaty udbhramati pramīlati pataty udyāti mūrcchaty api |
children.translated_text: She gets goosebumps, she shivers, she laments, she trembles, she faints; she meditates, she wanders deliriously, she swoons, she falls, she rises, she even loses consciousness —

children.text: etāvaty atanu-jvare vara-tanur jīven na kiṃ te rasāt svar-vaidya-pratima prasīdasi yadi tyakto'nyathā hastakaḥ || GG_4.19 ||
children.translated_text: With such a violent fever of love, would this beautiful body not survive through your essence? If you, who are like the divine physician, are gracious — otherwise the case is beyond help. || GG_4.19 ||
Afflicted by love, [she is] curable only by the nectar of contact with your body, O divine physician dear [to us];

children.text: nivṛtta-bādhāṃ kuruṣe na rādhām upendra-vajrād api dāruṇo'si || GG_4.20 ||
children.translated_text: You do not free <s>Rādhā</s> from affliction — you are more cruel than the thunderbolt of <s>Upendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). || GG_4.20 ||

children.text: kandarpa-jvara-saṃjvarātura-tanor aścaryam asyāś ciraṃ cetaś candana-candramaḥ-kamalinī-cintāsu santāmyati |
children.translated_text: It is a wonder that the mind of her, whose body is afflicted with the raging fever of <s>Kāma</s>, has long been distressed by thoughts of sandalwood, moonlight, and lotuses;

children.text: kintu klānti-vaśena śītala-tanuṃ tvām ekam eva priyaṃ dhyāyantī rahasi sthitā katham api kṣīṇā kṣaṇaṃ prāṇiti || GG_4.21 ||
children.translated_text: But, overpowered by exhaustion, meditating on you alone, her cool-bodied beloved, remaining in solitude, somehow she barely breathes, wasted away. || GG_4.21 ||

children.text: kṣaṇam api virahaḥ purā na sehe nayana-nimīlana-khinnayā yayā te |
children.translated_text: She who formerly could not endure separation from you even for a moment, troubled even by the closing of her eyes —

children.text: śvasiti katham asau rasāla-śākhāṃ cira-viraheṇa vilokya puṣpitāgram || GG_4.22 ||
children.translated_text: How does she still breathe, seeing the mango branch with flowering tips after so long a separation? || GG_4.22 ||

children.text: vṛṣṭi-vyākula-gokula-vana-rasād uddhṛtya govardhanaṃ bibhrad ballava-vallabhābhir adhikānandāc ciraṃ cumbitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having lifted <s>Govardhana</s> [mountain] from the forest of <s>Gokula</s> distressed by rain, bearing [it], he was long kissed by the beloved cowherd women out of excessive joy;

children.text: darpeṇeva tad-arpitādhara-taṭī-sindūra-mudrāṅkito bāhur gopa-tanos tanotu bhavatāṃ śreyāṃsi kaṃsa-dviṣaḥ || GG_4.23 ||
children.translated_text: May the arm of the cowherd-bodied enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, as if proudly marked with the <s>sindūra</s> seal of their offered lip-edges, extend blessings to you. || GG_4.23 ||

body.text:
iti śrī-gīta-govinde snigdha-madhusūdano nāma
caturthaḥ sargaḥ
||4||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth canto named '<s>Snigdha-Madhusūdana</s>' (The Tender Slayer of <s>Madhu</s>) in the great poem <s>Gīta Govinda</s>. ||4||
(5) Fifth Canto: <s>Sākāṅkṣa-Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> (The Longing Lotus-Eyed One)

children.text: aham iha nivasāmi yāhi rādhām anunaya mad-vacanena cānayethāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I shall remain here; go to <s>Rādhā</s>, appease her with my words, and bring her' —

children.text: iti madhu-rīpuṇā sakhī niyuktā svayam idam etya punar jagāda rādhām || GG_5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Thus commissioned by the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, the friend herself, having come, spoke again to <s>Rādhā</s>. || GG_5.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 10 ||

children.translated_text: [This is] sung in <s>Deśīvarāḍi</s> <s>rāga</s> and <s>Rūpaka</s> <s>tāla</s>.
The <s>Malaya</s> breeze carries [spring], having placed <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) [within it];
It bursts forth in clusters of flowers, to break the hearts of those separated. || GG_5.2 ||

body.text: tava virahe vana-mālī sakhi sīdati | dhruva-padam ||
body.translated_text: In separation from you, the forest-garlanded one (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), O friend, languishes. || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: She burns in the cool rays [of the moon], she imitates death;
she falls at the arrow of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), she laments, growing ever more distressed. || GG_5.3 ||
When the swarm of bees hums, she covers her ears;

children.text: manasi kalita-virahe niśi nisi rujam upayāti || GG_5.4 ||
children.translated_text: with separation conceived in her mind, night after night she suffers pain. || GG_5.4 ||
She dwells in the canopy of the forest, she abandons her lovely home;

children.text: luṭhati dharaṇi-śayane bahu vilapati tava nāma || GG_5.5 ||
children.translated_text: she rolls on her bed upon the ground, lamenting greatly your name. || GG_5.5 ||
Thus sings the poet <s>Jayadeva</s>, through the play of separation;

children.text: manasi rabhasa-vibhave harir udayatu sukṛtena || GG_5.6 ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari</s>, whose splendor is passionate, arise in the heart through good deeds. || GG_5.6 ||

body.translated_text: [Section break]

children.text: pūrvaṃ yatra samaṃ tvayā rati-pater āsāditāḥ siddhayas tasminn eva nikuñja-manmatha-mahā-tīrthe punar mādhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: In that very bower — that great pilgrimage site of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) — where previously together with you the perfections of the god of love were attained, <s>Mādhava</s> once again,

children.text: dhyāyaṃs tvām aniśaṃ japann api tavaivālāpa-mantrāvaliṃ bhūyas tvat-kuca-kumbha-nirbhara-parīrambhāmṛtaṃ vāñchati || GG_5.7 ||
children.translated_text: meditating on you ceaselessly, murmuring the rosary of mantras that are your words, desires once more the nectar of a full embrace of your pitcher-like breasts. || GG_5.7 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 11 ||

children.translated_text: It is sung in <s>Gurjarī</s> rāga with <s>Ekatālī</s> tāla.
He who has gone to the tryst, the essence of love's delight, dressed in an attire captivating to <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) —

children.text: na kuru nitambini gamana-vilambanam anusara taṃ hṛdayeśam || GG_5.8 ||
children.translated_text: O beautiful-hipped one, do not delay your going — follow him, the lord of your heart. || GG_5.8 ||
In the gentle breeze, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the forest dwells the one garlanded with forest flowers (<s>Vanamālī</s>),
his pair of hands restless for caressing the region of your full breasts. || Refrain ||
[Editorial note:]

children.text: {This line does not seem to be in all versions. Prabodhananda does not comment on it.}
children.translated_text: [This line does not seem to be in all versions. <s>Prabodhananda</s> does not comment on it.]
He plays the soft flute, calling your name, having made the appointed signal;

children.text: bahu manute'tanu te tanu-saṅgata-pavana-calitam api reṇum || GG_5.9 ||
children.translated_text: he greatly treasures, O slender one, even the dust stirred by the wind that has touched your body. || GG_5.9 ||
When a bird alights, when a leaf stirs, he suspects your arrival;

children.text: racayati śayanaṃ sacakita-nayanaṃ paśyati tava panthānam || GG_5.10 ||
children.translated_text: he prepares the bed and with startled eyes gazes upon your path. || GG_5.10 ||

children.text: mukharam adhīraṃ tyaja mañjīraṃ ripum iva keli-sulolam |
children.translated_text: Cast off the jingling, impatient anklet, that enemy of love's sport, as it were;

children.text: cala sakhi kuñjaṃ satimira-puñjaṃ śīlaya nīla-nicolam || GG_5.11 ||
children.translated_text: go, O friend, to the bower thick with darkness, and don the dark blue garment. || GG_5.11 ||

children.text: urasi murārer upahita-hāre ghana iva tarala-balāke |
children.translated_text: On the chest of <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), upon his necklace — like a cloud with trembling cranes,

children.text: taḍid iva pīte rati-viparīte rājasi sukṛta-vipāke || GG_5.12 ||
children.translated_text: like lightning upon yellow [garments], in the reversal of love-play, you will shine, O fruit of good deeds. || GG_5.12 ||
Arrange a covering for your hips, whose garment has slipped and whose girdle has come undone;

children.text: kiśalaya-śayane paṅkaja-nayane nidhim iva harṣa-nidhānam || GG_5.13 ||
children.translated_text: on the bed of tender sprouts, O lotus-eyed one, [place] a treasure-house of joy, as it were. || GG_5.13 ||

children.text: harir abhimāṇī rajanir idānīm iyam api yāti virāmam |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> waits with longing, and this night too is drawing to a close;

children.text: kuru mama vacanaṃ satvara-racanaṃ pūraya madhu-ripu-kāmam || GG_5.14 ||
children.translated_text: heed my words, make haste in your preparations, and fulfill the desire of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>. || GG_5.14 ||
Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>, who serves <s>Hari</s>, sings this supremely beautiful [song];

children.text: pramudita-hṛdayaṃ harim atisadayaṃ namata sukṛta-kamanīyaṃ || GG_5.15 ||
children.translated_text: bow to <s>Hari</s>, joyful of heart, exceedingly compassionate, beautiful through good deeds. || GG_5.15 ||

body.translated_text: [Section break]

children.text: vikirati muhuḥ śvāsān āśāḥ puro muhur īkṣate praviśati muhuḥ kuñjaṃ gūñjan muhur bahu tāmyati |
children.translated_text: He scatters sighs again and again, gazes at the horizon again and again, enters the bower humming again and again, languishes greatly again and again,

children.text: racayati muhuḥ śayyāṃ paryākulaṃ muhur īkṣate madana-kadana-klāntaḥ kānte priyas tava vartate || GG_5.16 ||
children.translated_text: prepares the bed again and again, looks about in agitation again and again — tormented by the afflictions of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), your beloved, O dear one, remains thus. || GG_5.16 ||

children.text: tvad-vāmyena samaṃ samagram adhunā tigmāṃśur astaṃ gato govindasya manorathena ca samaṃ prāptaṃ tamaḥ sāndratām |
children.translated_text: Together with your coyness, the fierce-rayed [sun] has now set; together with <s>Govinda</s>'s longing, the darkness has attained its deepest intensity;

children.text: kokānāṃ karuṇa-svanena sadṛśī dīrgha-mad-abhyarthanā tan mugdhe viphalaṃ vilambanam asau ramyo'bhisāra-kṣaṇaḥ || GG_5.17 ||
children.translated_text: like my prolonged entreaties, the piteous cries of the <s>Cakravāka</s> birds [resound] — therefore, O innocent one, this delay is in vain; this is the delightful moment for the tryst. || GG_5.17 ||

children.text: āśleṣād anu cumbanād anu nakho-lekhād anu svāntaja-prodbodhād anu sambhramād anu ratārambhād anu prītayoḥ |
children.translated_text: After the embrace, after the kiss, after the nail-marks, after the awakening of desire born in the heart, after the excitement, after the commencement of love-making — of those two lovers

children.text: anyārthaṃ gatayor bhramān militayoḥ sambhāṣaṇair jānator dampatyor iha ko na ko na tamasi vrīḍā-vimiśro rasaḥ || GG_5.18 ||
children.translated_text: who went for different purposes, who met by chance, who recognized [each other] through conversation — what husband and wife here, what [couple] in the darkness, does not have a sentiment mingled with modesty? || GG_5.18 ||

children.text: sa-bhaya-cakitaṃ vinyasyantīṃ dṛśaṃ timire pathi pratitaru muhuḥ sthitvā mandaṃ padāni vitanvatīm |
children.translated_text: As she places her gaze fearfully and timidly upon the dark path, stopping at every tree, slowly extending her steps,

children.text: katham api rahaḥ prāptām aṅgair anaṅga-taraṇgibhiḥ sumukhi subhagaḥ paśyan sa tvām upaitu kṛtārthatām || GG_5.19 ||
children.translated_text: having somehow reached the secret place with limbs rippling with the waves of <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless god of love) — O beautiful-faced one, may that blessed one, seeing you, attain the fulfillment of his desire. || GG_5.19 ||
<s>Rādhā</s>'s innocent lotus-face is his bee; the crest-jewel of the three worlds, a dark sapphire fit for the adornment of the directions' beauty; the destroyer of the earth's burden,

children.text: svacchandaṃ vraja-sundarī-jana-manas-toṣa-pradoṣodayaḥ kaṃsa-dhvaṃsana-dhūma-ketur avatu tvāṃ devakī-nandanaḥ || GG_5.20 ||
children.translated_text: freely giving delight to the minds of the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s> at the rising of dusk — may <s>Devakī</s>'s son, the comet that destroyed <s>Kaṃsa</s>, protect you. || GG_5.20 ||

body.text:
iti śrī-gīta-govinde'bhisārikā-varṇane sākāṅkṣa-puṇḍarīkākso nāma
pañcamaḥ sargaḥ
||5||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the Śrī Gīta Govinda, in the description of the heroine going to meet her lover, [this is] the fifth canto named "Sākāṅkṣa-Puṇḍarīkākṣa" (The Lotus-Eyed One Full of Longing). ||5||

body.translated_text: Sixth Canto: "Sotkaṇṭha-Vaikuṇṭha" (The Anxious <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>).

children.text: atha tāṃ gantum aśaktāṃ ciram anuraktāṃ latā-gṛhe dṛṣṭvā |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing her unable to go [to the tryst], long enamored, in the bower of creepers,

children.text: tac-caritaṃ govinde manasija-mande sakhī prāha || GG_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: her friend spoke to <s>Govinda</s>, who was languid with desire, about her condition. || GG_6.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 12 ||

children.translated_text: It is sung in <s>Guṇakarī</s> rāga with <s>Rūpaka</s> tāla.
She sees you in every direction, in secret,
drinking the sweet honey of your lips. || GG_6.2 ||

body.text: nātha hare sīdati rādhā vāsa-gṛhe || dhru. ||
body.translated_text: O Lord <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> languishes in her dwelling. || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: In her eagerness to come to meet you, she stumbles,
and falls after taking but a few steps. || GG_6.3 ||
Having fashioned bracelets of bright lotus-fiber sprouts,

children.text: jīvati param iha tava rati-kalayā || GG_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: she lives only by the art of your love-making. || GG_6.4 ||
She gazes again and again at her adornments playfully,
cultivating the thought, "I am the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)." || GG_6.5 ||
"Why does he not swiftly come to the tryst?"

children.text: harir iti vadati sakhīm anuvāram || GG_6.6 ||
children.translated_text: She says to her friend "<s>Hari</s>!" again and again. || GG_6.6 ||
She embraces and kisses the thick darkness

children.text: harir upagata iti timiram analpam || GG_6.7 ||
children.translated_text: as if <s>Hari</s> had come — [darkness] resembling a rain-cloud. || GG_6.7 ||
When you delay, she loses all shame;
she laments and weeps, dressed and ready for your visit. || GG_6.8 ||
This is uttered by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>, the poet;
may it render the hearts of connoisseurs exceedingly joyful. || GG_6.9 ||

body.translated_text: [Section break]

children.translated_text: With abundant goosebumps, with intensified sighs, with inner paralysis, with a voice choked and agitated by distress — speaking thus,

children.text: tava kitava vidhāyāmanda-kandarpa-cintāṃ rasa-jala-nidhi-magnā dhyāna-lagnā mṛgakṣī || GG_6.10 ||
children.translated_text: O deceiver, having created for her the boundless anxiety of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), the doe-eyed one is immersed in the ocean of passion, absorbed in meditation [upon you]. || GG_6.10 ||

children.text: aṅgeṣv ābharaṇaṃ karoti bahuśaḥ patre'pi sañcāriṇī prāptaṃ tvāṃ pariśaṅkate vitanute śayyāṃ ciraṃ dhyāyati |
children.translated_text: She puts ornaments on her limbs again and again, starts at every moving leaf, suspects you have arrived, prepares the bed, and meditates long;

children.text: ity ākalpa-vikalpa-talpa-racanā-saṅkalpa-līlā-śata-vyāsaktāpi vinā tvayā vara-tanur naiṣā niśāṃ neṣyati || GG_6.11 ||
children.translated_text: thus engaged in a hundred playful fantasies of dressing, imagining, and arranging the couch — yet even so, without you, this beautiful-bodied one will not endure the night. || GG_6.11 ||

children.text: kiṃ viśrāmyasi kṛṣṇa-bhogi-bhavane bhāṇḍīra-bhūmī-ruhi bhrātar yāsi na dṛṣṭi-gocaram itaḥ sānanda-nandāspadam |
children.translated_text: "Why do you rest in the abode of the black serpent (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-bhogi)? O brother, do you not go to the great <s>Bhaṇḍīra</s> tree within sight from here, the joyful abode of <s>Nanda</s>?"

children.text: rādhāyā vacanaṃ tad adhvaga-mukhān nandāntike gopato govindasya jayanti sāyam atithi-prāśastya-garbhā giraḥ || GG_6.12 ||
children.translated_text: These words of <s>Rādhā</s>, [heard] from the mouths of travelers, [reaching] <s>Nanda</s>, among the cowherds, toward <s>Govinda</s> at evening — prevail as speeches pregnant with the praise of a guest. || GG_6.12 ||

body.text:
iti śrī-gīta-govinde'bhisārikā-varṇane dhanya-vaikuṇṭho nāma
ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ
||6||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the Śrī Gīta Govinda, in the description of the heroine going to meet her lover, [this is] the sixth canto named "Dhanya-Vaikuṇṭha" (The Blessed <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>). ||6||
Seventh Canto: "Nāgara-Nārāyaṇa" (The Urbane <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>).

children.text: vṛndāvanāntaram adīpayad aṃśu-jālair dik-sundarī-vadana-candana-bindur induḥ || GG_7.1 ||
children.translated_text: illuminating the interior of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> with its clusters of rays — the moon, a dot of sandalwood paste on the face of the beauty of the directions. || GG_7.1 ||

body.translated_text: Meanwhile, as if a sin born from the path of the assembly of unchaste women, [the moon rose] with the beauty of its clear markings,

children.text: prasarati śaśa-dhara-bimbe vihita-vilambe ca mādhave vidhurā |
children.translated_text: As the moon's disc spread forth, and as <s>Mādhava</s> delayed,
the distressed one composed various lamentations, loudly, with great anguish. || GG_7.2 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 13 ||

children.translated_text: It is sung in <s>Mālava</s> rāga with <s>Yati</s> tāla.
[Editorial note:]
["pratimaṇṭha-"]

children.text: kathita-samaye'pi harir ahaha na yayau vanam |
children.translated_text: At the appointed time <s>Hari</s> did not come to the forest — alas!

children.text: mama viphalam idam amala-rūpam api yauvanam || GG_7.3 ||
children.translated_text: This unblemished beauty and youth of mine is in vain. || GG_7.3 ||

body.text: yāmi he kam iha śaraṇaṃ sakhī-jana-vacana-vañcitā ||dhruva||||
body.translated_text: To whom shall I go for refuge here, deceived by the words of my friends? || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: For following him at night, even the dense forest was traversed;

children.text: tena mama hṛdayam idam asama-śara-kīlitam || GG_7.4 ||
children.translated_text: by that, this heart of mine is pierced by the unequal arrows [of <s>Kāma</s>]. || GG_7.4 ||

body.text: mama maraṇam eva varam iti vitatha-ketanā |

children.text: kim iha viṣahāmi virahānalam acetanā || GG_7.5 ||
children.translated_text: how can I endure the fire of separation, bereft of consciousness? || GG_7.5 ||

body.translated_text: "My death alone is preferable" — with such false resolve,

children.translated_text: Alas, this sweet, honey-like night torments me;
some fortunate woman of good deeds is enjoying <s>Hari</s>. || GG_7.6 ||
Alas, I consider my bracelets and jeweled ornaments
to be a great reproach, fanning the fire of separation from <s>Hari</s>. || GG_7.7 ||
Upon my body, tender as a flower, by the play of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (the bodiless god of love's) formidable arrows,

children.text: srag api hṛdi hanti mām ativiṣama-śilayā || GG_7.8 ||
children.translated_text: even a garland strikes my heart with exceedingly cruel force. || GG_7.8 ||
I dwell here, heedless of the forest reeds;

children.text: smarati madhusūdano mām api na cetasā || GG_7.9 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Madhusūdana</s> (the slayer of <s>Madhu</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) does not even think of me. || GG_7.9 ||
May the poetry of the poet <s>Jayadeva</s>, who takes refuge at the feet of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: vasatu hṛdi yuvatir iva komala-kalāvatī || GG_7.10 ||
children.translated_text: dwell in the heart like a young woman, tender and full of art. || GG_7.10 ||

body.translated_text: [Section break]

children.text: tat kiṃ kām api kāminīm abhisṛtaḥ kiṃ vā kalā-kelibhir baddho bandhubhir andhakāriṇi vanābhyarṇe kim udbhrāmyati |
children.translated_text: Has he then gone to some other woman? Or is he bound by the playful arts of his companions? Or does he wander in the forest near to the darkness?

children.text: kāntaḥ klānta-manā manāg api pathi prasthātum evākṣamaḥ saṅketī-kṛta-mañju-vāñjula-latā-kuñje'pi yan nāgataḥ || GG_7.11 ||
children.translated_text: The beloved, with a weary mind, unable even to set out a little upon the path — has not come to the bower of lovely <s>Vāñjula</s> (Ashoka) creepers appointed for the tryst. || GG_7.11 ||

children.text: athāgatāṃ mādhavam antareṇa sakhīm iyaṃ vīkṣya viṣāda-mūkām |
children.translated_text: Then, seeing her friend return without <s>Mādhava</s>, silent with dejection,

children.text: viśaṅkamānā ramitaṃ kayāpi janārdanaṃ dṛṣṭavad etad āha || GG_7.12 ||
children.translated_text: she suspected that <s>Janārdana</s> had dallied with someone else, and as if having seen it, spoke thus: || GG_7.12 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 14 ||

children.translated_text: It is sung in <s>Vasanta</s> rāga with <s>Yati</s> tāla.
Dressed in attire befitting the battle of love,
her hair loosened, with fallen flowers, slightly disheveled — || GG_7.13 ||

body.translated_text: some woman of surpassing virtues sports with the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). || Refrain ||
