her necklace trembling upon the pitcher-like breasts. || GG_7.14 ||

body.translated_text: Altered in form from <s>Hari</s>'s embrace,

children.translated_text: Her moon-like face lovely with disheveled locks,
drowsy from the eager drinking of his lips. || GG_7.15 ||
Her cheeks marked by swaying earrings,
her girdle jingling, her hips swaying with a playful gait. || GG_7.16 ||
Smiling bashfully under the gaze of her beloved,
cooing in many ways with the savoring of love's passion. || GG_7.17 ||
With abundant goosebumps, with broad trembling and quivering,
with sighs, with eyes closed, with blossoming desire. || GG_7.18 ||
Her beautiful body laden with drops of the sweat of exertion,
fallen upon his chest, steadfast in the battle of love. || GG_7.19 ||
Described by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s> is <s>Hari</s>'s love-sport;
may it quell the impurity of the <s>Kali</s> age. || GG_7.20 ||

body.translated_text: [Section break]

children.translated_text: The lustre of <s>Murāri</s>'s (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s) lotus-face, pale with separation, though concealing the pain,

children.text: vidhur atīva tanoti mano-bhuvaḥ suhṛd aye hṛdaye madana-vyathām || GG_7.21 ||
children.translated_text: this moon, O friend, exceedingly extends in the heart the agony of love inflicted by <s>Manobhū</s> (the god of love). || GG_7.21 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 15 ||

children.translated_text: It is sung in <s>Gurjarī</s> rāga with <s>Ekatālī</s> tāla.
On the face of his beloved, with desire aroused, he kisses and turns her lips,

children.text: mṛga-mada-tilakaṃ likhati sapulakaṃ mṛgam iva rajanī-kare || GG_7.22 ||
children.translated_text: and draws a <s>mṛgamada</s> (musk) <s>tilaka</s> mark, with goosebumps [rising], as if [drawing] a deer upon the moon. || GG_7.22 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) now sports victorious on the sandy banks of the <s>Yamunā</s> forest. || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: On her beautiful hair, dark as a mass of clouds, upon her youthful trembling face,
he places a <s>Kurubaka</s> (red amaranth) flower, restless and lovely, as if [placing] the deer in the hunting ground of the god of love. || GG_7.23 ||
On the firmament of her close-pressed breasts, anointed with the lustre of musk,
he places a necklace of pure gems — a constellation of stars — adorned with nail-mark moons. || GG_7.24 ||
On her tender pair of arms, surpassing lotus stalks, on her palm like a lotus petal,
he places emerald bracelets — a swarm of bees — cool as snow. || GG_7.25 ||
On her hips, the abode of love-play, ample and without blemish — the golden throne of <s>Manasija</s> (the mind-born god of love) —
he scatters a jeweled girdle, laughing like a <s>toraṇa</s> (ornamental arch), having made it fragrant. || GG_7.26 ||
On her sprout-like feet, the abode of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), honored by clusters of nail-gems,

children.text: bahir-apavaraṇaṃ yāvaka-bharaṇaṃ janayati hṛdi yojite || GG_7.27 ||
children.translated_text: he applies <s>yāvaka</s> (lac-dye) as an outer covering, placing [it] on the heart. || GG_7.27 ||

children.text: ramayati subhṛśaṃ kam api sudṛśaṃ khala-haladhara-sodare |
children.translated_text: He delights some beautiful woman exceedingly — the brother of the wicked <s>Haladhara</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>, the plough-bearer);

children.text: kim aphalam avasaṃ ciram iha virasaṃ vada sakhi viṭapodare || GG_7.28 ||
children.translated_text: why do I dwell here fruitlessly, without joy for so long? Tell me, O friend, in the hollow of this tree. || GG_7.28 ||
In this narration of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), in this celebration of <s>Hari</s>'s qualities, [for] the servant of the feet of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>,

children.text: kali-yuga-caritaṃ na vasatu duritaṃ kavi-nṛpa-jayadevake || GG_7.29 ||
children.translated_text: may the impurity of the <s>Kali</s> age not abide in the poet-king <s>Jayadeva</s>. || GG_7.29 ||
[Editorial note:]
["racitam" is seen in some [manuscripts].]

body.translated_text: [Section break]

children.text: nāyātaḥ sakhi nirdayo yadi śaṭhas tvaṃ dūti kiṃ dūyase svacchandaṃ bahu-vallabhaḥ sa ramate kiṃ tatra te dūṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: "He has not come, the cruel scoundrel" — O friend, O messenger, why do you grieve? He of many beloveds sports freely — what fault of yours is there in that?

children.text: paśyādya priya-saṅgamāya dayitasyākṛṣyamāṇaṃ guṇair utkaṇṭhārti-bharād iva sphuṭad idaṃ cetaḥ svayam yāsyati || GG_7.30 ||
children.translated_text: Behold now: for the sake of union with the beloved, this heart, drawn by his virtues, as if bursting from the weight of the agony of longing, will go of its own accord. || GG_7.30 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 16 ||

children.translated_text: It is sung in <s>Deśavarāḍī</s> rāga with <s>Rūpaka</s> tāla.
She is not cooled by the lotus-eyes trembling with breeze,
nor by a bed of tender sprouts. || GG_7.31 ||

body.translated_text: She who was loved by the one garlanded with forest flowers (<s>Vanamālī</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), O friend — || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: With a face lovely as a blossoming lotus,
she does not burst open [even] from the arrows of <s>Manasija</s> (the Love god, born of the mind). || GG_7.32 ||
With speech sweeter than nectar, most tender,
she does not burn [even] from the sandal-scented breeze. || GG_7.33 ||
With feet beautiful as lotuses growing on land and water,
she does not roll about [even] from the rays of the moon. || GG_7.34 ||
With [a complexion] radiant as a gathering of rain-laden clouds,

children.text: dalati na sā hṛdi cira-viraheṇa || GG_7.35 ||
children.translated_text: she does not break apart in her heart [even] from prolonged separation. || GG_7.35 ||
NOTE:
{"viraha-bhareṇa" (with the burden of separation) is the reading in <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition.}
With a garment pure and brilliant as the touchstone of gold,
she does not sigh [even] from the laughter of her companions. || GG_7.36 ||
By him who is the finest youth among all the people of the world,

children.text: vahati na sā rujam atikaruṇena || GG_7.37 ||
children.translated_text: she does not bear affliction, [though] he is most compassionate. || GG_7.37 ||
By the words composed by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>,

children.text: praviśatu harir api hṛdayam anena || GG_7.38 ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari</s> himself enter [your] heart through this [song]. || GG_7.38 ||

children.text: mano-bhavānandana candanānila prasīda re dakṣiṇa muñca vāmatām |
children.translated_text: O wind bearing sandalwood fragrance, delight of the Love god, O southern breeze, be gracious — abandon your cruelty! For a moment, O life-breath of the world, bring <s>Mādhava</s> before me, [or else] you will become the destroyer of my life. || GG_7.39 ||

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ jagat-prāṇa nidāya mādhavaṃ puro mama prāṇa-haro bhaviṣyasi || GG_7.39 ||
children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"nidhāya" (having placed) is
an
alternate
reading.}

children.text: ripur iva sakhi-saṃvāso'yaṃ śikhīva himānilo viṣam iva sudhā-raśmir yasmin dunoti mano-gate |
children.translated_text: The companionship of friends is like an enemy; the southern breeze is like a frost wind; the moon's nectar-rays are like poison — when he, the mind-born [Love], is present; my heart, O merciless one, does not turn away from him again by force.

children.text: hṛdayam adaye tasmin naivaṃ punar valate balāt kuvalaya-dṛśāṃ vāmaḥ kāmo nikāma-niraṇkuśaḥ || GG_7.40 ||
children.translated_text: Perverse is <s>Kāma</s> (Love), utterly unrestrained, toward the lotus-eyed women. || GG_7.40 ||

children.text: bādhāṃ vidhehi malayānila pañca-bāṇa prāṇān gṛhāṇa na gṛhaṃ punar āśrayiṣye |
children.translated_text: Go ahead, O Malaya breeze, inflict harm! O five-arrowed [<s>Kāma</s>], take my life — I shall not seek shelter in a home again!

children.text: kiṃ te kṛtānta-bhagini kṣamayā taraṅgair aṅgāni siñca mama śāmyatu deha-dāhaḥ || GG_7.41 ||
children.translated_text: O sister of death, why [this show of] patience? Sprinkle my limbs with your waves — let this burning of my body be extinguished! || GG_7.41 ||

children.text: prātar nīla-nicolam acyutam uraḥ saṃvīta-pītāṃśukaṃ rādhāyāś cakitaṃ vilokya hasati svairaṃ sakhi-maṇḍale |
children.translated_text: At dawn, seeing <s>Acyuta</s>, his chest dark as a blue sapphire, wearing a yellow garment, startled, <s>Rādhā</s>'s circle of friends laughs freely.

children.text: vrīḍā-cañcalam añcalaṃ nayanayor ādhāya rādhānane svādu-smera-mukho'yam astu jagad-ānandāya nandātmajaḥ || GG_7.42 ||
children.translated_text: Placing the restless end of her garment over <s>Rādhā</s>'s eyes on her face, may this son of <s>Nanda</s>, with a sweetly smiling countenance, bring joy to the world! || GG_7.42 ||

body.text:
iti śrī-gīta-govinda-mahākāvye vipralabdhā-varṇane
nāgara-nārāyaṇo nāma
saptamaḥ sargaḥ
||7||
body.translated_text:
Thus in the great poem Śrī Gīta Govinda, in the description of the deceived woman (<s>Vipralabdhā</s>),
[this is] the seventh canto named "<s>Nāgara-Nārāyaṇa</s>" (The Urbane <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>).
||7||

(8)
Eighth Canto
<s>Vilakṣa-Lakṣmīpati</s> (The Abashed Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>)

children.text: atha katham api yāminīṃ vinīya smara-śara-jarjaritāpi sā prabhāte |
children.translated_text: Then, having somehow passed through the night, though pierced by the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (Love), at dawn,

children.text: anunaya-vacanaṃ vadantam agre praṇatam api priyaṃ āha sābhyasūyam || GG_8.1 ||
children.translated_text: she spoke to her beloved who stood before her saying conciliatory words and bowing — she spoke with jealous reproach. || GG_8.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 17 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Bhairavī</s> rāga and <s>Yati</s> tāla.
Her eyes, reddened with the passion born of long wakefulness through the night, languidly half-closed,

children.text: vahati nayanam anurāgam iva sphuṭam udita-rasābhiniveśam || GG_8.2 ||
children.translated_text: reveal her love as if openly, with a clearly arisen intensity of feeling. || GG_8.2 ||

children.text: hari hari yāhi mādhava yāhi keśava mā vada kaitava-vādam |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>! Go, <s>Mādhava</s>, go, <s>Keśava</s> — do not speak deceitful words!

children.text: tām anusara sarasīruha-locana yā tava harati viṣādam || dhru. ||
children.translated_text: Follow her, O lotus-eyed one, who takes away your sorrow. || Refrain ||
The collyrium-darkened [marks] on [your] eyes, [left by] kissing — creating a dark blue appearance,

children.text: daśana-vasanam aruṇ aṃ tava krsṇa tanoti tanor anurūpam || GG_8.3 ||
children.translated_text: and the reddened cloth at [your] teeth, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, reveal what befits your body. || GG_8.3 ||
Your body displays the marks of scratches from sharp nails in the battle of love,
like a record of the victory of passion inscribed with gold on a tablet of emerald. || GG_8.4 ||
This generous heart of yours, stained with red lac flowing from [her] lotus-feet,
seems to display outwardly the fresh sprouts of the tree of <s>Madana</s> (Love). || GG_8.5 ||

children.text: daśana-padaṃ bhavad-adhara-gataṃ mama janayati cetasi khedam |
children.translated_text: The tooth-marks on your lower lip generate grief in my heart —

children.text: kathayati katham adhunāpi mayā saha tava vapur etad abhedam || GG_8.6 ||
children.translated_text: how can you now claim that your body is still one with mine? || GG_8.6 ||

children.text: bahir iva malinataraṃ tava kṛṣṇa mano'pi bhaviṣyati nūnam |
children.translated_text: As your exterior is darkened, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, so surely your mind will also be,

children.text: katham atha vañcayase janam anugatam asama-śara-jvara-dūnam || GG_8.7 ||
children.translated_text: for how else do you deceive a person devoted [to you], afflicted by the fever of the unequaled-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>]? || GG_8.7 ||

children.text: bhramati bhavān abalā-kavalāya vaneṣu kim atra vicitram |
children.translated_text: You wander in the forests to devour helpless women — what is surprising in this?
Even <s>Pūtanā</s> reveals [your] childhood behavior, merciless in the killing of women. || GG_8.8 ||
The lament of the <s>Khaṇḍitā</s> (woman wronged by her lover), cheated of love, as composed by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s> —

children.text: śṛṇuta sudhā-madhuraṃ vibudhā vibudhālayato'pi durāpam || GG_8.9 ||
children.translated_text: listen, O wise ones, to this [song] sweet as nectar, unattainable even from the abode of the gods. || GG_8.9 ||

body.text: tavedaṃ paśyantyāḥ prasarad-anurāgaṃ bahir iva priyā-pādālakta-cchuritam aruṇa-cchāya-hṛdayam |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"dyoti-" [variant reading]}

children.text: mamādya prakhyāta-praṇaya-bhara-bhaṅgena kitava tvad-ālokaḥ śokād api kim api lajjāṃ janayati || GG_8.10 ||
children.translated_text: O deceiver, today the sight of you, through the destruction of my well-known burden of love, produces in me something beyond sorrow — even shame. || GG_8.10 ||

body.translated_text: As I behold this heart of yours, its rosy hue stained by the red lac from your beloved's feet, as if your spreading love were made visible outwardly —

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"vibhraṃśana" [variant reading]}
NOTE:
{"dṛpti" [variant reading]}

children.text: dṛpyad-dānava-dūyamāna-diviṣad-durvāra-duḥkhāpadāṃ bhraṃśaḥ kaṃsa-ripor vyapohayatu vaḥ śreyāṃsi vaṃśī-ravaḥ || GG_8.11 ||
children.translated_text: may the flute-song of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> dispel for you the fall into irremediable sorrows of the gods tormented by the arrogant demons! || GG_8.11 ||

body.translated_text: A great mantra for the doe-eyed women — causing inner enchantment, toppling of crowns, swaying of <s>Mandāra</s> flowers falling loosely, drawing to a standstill, delighting the eyes —

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"vyapolayatu vaḥ śreyāṃsi" is
an
alternate

body.text:
iti śrī-śrī-gīta-govinde mahā-kāvye khaṇḍitā-varṇane
vilakṣa-lakṣmīpatir nāma
aṣṭamaḥ sargaḥ
||8||
body.translated_text: reading.}

Thus in the great poem Śrī Śrī Gīta Govinda, in the description of the wronged woman (<s>Khaṇḍitā</s>),
[this is] the eighth canto named "<s>Vilakṣa-Lakṣmīpati</s>" (The Abashed Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>).
||8||

(9)
Ninth Canto
<s>Mugdha-Mukunda</s> (The Bewildered <s>Mukunda</s>)

children.translated_text: Then, to her who was afflicted by <s>Manmatha</s> (Love), shattered by the taste of love, overcome by despondency,

children.text: anucintita-hari-caritāṃ kalahāntaritām uvāca rahasi sakhī || GG_9.1 ||
children.translated_text: meditating on <s>Hari</s>'s deeds, estranged after a quarrel — her friend spoke to her in private. || GG_9.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 18 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Gurjarī</s> rāga and <s>Yati</s> tāla.
<s>Hari</s> comes to meet you as the spring breeze carries the fragrance of honey —

children.text: kim aparam adhika-sukhaṃ sakhi bhavane || GG_9.2 ||
children.translated_text: what greater happiness, O friend, could there be in [your] home? || GG_9.2 ||

body.text: mādhave mā kuru mānini mānam aye || dhruva-padam ||
body.translated_text: Do not maintain your pride toward <s>Mādhava</s>, O proud one! || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: Heavier even than a palmyra fruit, exceedingly juicy —
why do you make your pitcher-like breasts fruitless? || GG_9.3 ||

children.text: kati na kathitam idam anupadam aciram |
children.translated_text: How many times has this been told to you, again and again, without delay —
do not abandon <s>Hari</s>, who is supremely beautiful! || GG_9.4 ||
Why do you despair? Why do you weep, helpless?
The entire assembly of young women laughs at you! || GG_9.5 ||
NOTE:
{"śītala-" (cool) [variant reading]}
behold <s>Hari</s> and make your eyes fruitful! || GG_9.6 ||

body.translated_text: On a bed made of fresh, dewy lotus petals,

children.translated_text: Why do you produce such heavy sorrow in your mind?
Hear my words, free from [any] selfish motive. || GG_9.7 ||
Let <s>Hari</s> come near and speak many sweet words —

children.text: kim iti karoṣi hṛdayam atividhuram || GG_9.8 ||
children.translated_text: why do you make [your] heart so desolate? || GG_9.8 ||
The tale of <s>Hari</s> as composed by Śrī <s>Jayadeva</s>, most delicate,
may it delight the hearts of connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). || GG_9.9 ||

children.text: snigdhe yat paruṣāsi praṇamati stabdhāsi yad rāgiṇi dveṣa-sthāsi yad unmukhe vimukhatāṃ yātāsi tasmin priye |
children.translated_text: You are harsh to one who is tender, you are rigid to one who bows, you harbor hostility toward one who is passionate, you have turned away from one who faces you eagerly — toward that beloved one.

children.text: tad yuktaṃ viparīta-kāriṇi tava śrīkhaṇḍa-carcā viṣaṃ śītāṃśus tapano himaṃ hutavahaḥ krīḍā-mudo yātanāḥ || GG_9.10 ||
children.translated_text: This is fitting for you, O contrary one: sandalwood paste is poison, the cool-rayed moon is the scorching sun, snow is fire, the pleasures of play are tortures. || GG_9.10 ||

By the hosts of gods led by <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), filled with intense bliss, bowing with great reverence, the sapphire-like jewels of their foremost crowns reflecting the bees [at his feet],

children.text: svacchandaṃ makaranda-sundara-galan-mandākinī-meduraṃ śrī-govinda-padāravindam aśubha-skandāya vandāmahe || GG_9.11 ||
children.translated_text: freely flowing with the beautiful nectar of the <s>Mandākinī</s> (heavenly Ganges), rich with honey — we praise the lotus feet of Śrī <s>Govinda</s> for the destruction of all inauspiciousness! || GG_9.11 ||

body.translated_text:
Tenth Canto
<s>Catura-Caturbhuja</s> (The Clever Four-Armed One)

children.translated_text: Meanwhile, approaching the beautiful-faced one who was under the sway of fading anger, whose face was overcome with endless sighs, at the close of day,

children.text: savrīḍam īkṣita-sakhī-vadanāṃ dinānte sānanda-gadgada-padaṃ harir ity uvaca || GG_10.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> spoke with shy glances toward her friend's face, his words faltering with joy and emotion. || GG_10.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 19 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Deśavarāḍi</s> rāga and <s>Aṣṭatālī</s> tāla.

children.text: vadasi yadi kiñcid api danta-ruci-kaumudī harati dara-timiram atighoram |
children.translated_text: If you speak even a little, the moonlight of your teeth's radiance dispels the terrible darkness;

children.text: sphurad-adhara-sīdhave tava vadana-candramā rocayatu locana-cakoraṃ || GG_10.2 ||
children.translated_text: may the moon of your face, with its flowing nectar from your lips, delight the <s>cakora</s> birds of [my] eyes! || GG_10.2 ||

children.text: priye cāru-śīle muñca mayi mānam anidānaṃ |
children.translated_text: O beloved, of gracious disposition, abandon your groundless anger toward me!
The fire of <s>Madana</s> (Love) burns my mind instantly —
grant me the nectar-drink of your lotus-face! || Refrain ||

children.text: satyam evāsi yadi sudati mayi kopinī dehi khara-nakhara-śara-ghātam |
children.translated_text: If truly you are angry with me, O beautiful-toothed one, then inflict the blow of your sharp nail-arrows!

children.text: ghaṭaya bhuja-bandhanaṃ janaya rada-khaṇḍanaṃ yena vā bhavati sukha-jātaṃ || GG_10.3 ||
children.translated_text: Tighten the embrace of your arms, make the biting of your teeth — whatever brings forth pleasure! || GG_10.3 ||

children.text: tvam asi mama bhūṣaṇaṃ tvam asi mama jīvanaṃ tvam asi mama bhava-jaladhi-ratnam |
children.translated_text: You are my ornament, you are my life, you are the jewel of my ocean of existence;

children.text: bhavatu bhavatīha mayi satatam anurodhinī tatra mama hṛdayam atiyatnaṃ || GG_10.4 ||
children.translated_text: may you always be devoted to me here — in that my heart strives with utmost effort. || GG_10.4 ||

children.text: nīla-nalinābham api tanvi tava locanaṃ dhārayati kokanada-rūpaṃ |
children.translated_text: O slender one, your eye, though resembling a blue lotus, takes on the form of a red lotus;

children.text: kusuma-śara-bāṇa-bhāvena yadi rañjayasi kṛṣṇam idam etad-anurūpam || GG_10.5 ||
children.translated_text: if you tinge <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with the sentiment of the flower-arrowed one's [<s>Kāma</s>'s] arrows, this is entirely fitting. || GG_10.5 ||

children.text: sphuratu kuca-kumbhayor upari maṇi-mañjarī rañjayatu tava hṛdaya-deśam |
children.translated_text: May a garland of jewels shine upon the pitchers of your breasts, delighting the region of your heart;

children.text: rasatu raśanāpi tava ghana-jaghana-maṇḍale ghoṣayatu manmatha-nideśam || GG_10.6 ||
children.translated_text: may your girdle-chain resound upon the ample circle of your hips, proclaiming the commands of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love)! || GG_10.6 ||
Surpassing the lotus on land, delighting my heart, achieving the highest distinction in the arena of love —

children.text: bhaṇa masṛṇa-vāṇi karavāṇi caraṇa-dvayaṃ sarasa-lasad-alaktaka-rāgam || GG_10.7 ||
children.translated_text: speak, O soft-voiced one, and I shall adorn your two feet with the liquid splendor of red lac. || GG_10.7 ||

body.text: smara-garala-khaṇḍanaṃ mama śirasi maṇḍanaṃ dehi pada-pallavam udāram |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"dhehi" (place) is
an
alternate

children.text: jvalati mayi dāruṇo madana-kadanāruṇo haratu tad-upāhita-vikāram || GG_10.8 ||
children.translated_text: reading.} The fierce, crimson torment of Love blazes within me — let it remove the distortion inflicted by that [passion]! || GG_10.8 ||

body.translated_text: O grant me the tender sprouts of your feet upon my head — the antidote to Love's poison, the ornament upon my crown!

children.text: iti caṭula-cāṭu-paṭu-cāru mura-vairiṇo rādhikām adhi vacana-jātam |
children.translated_text: Thus the restless, flattering, eloquent, charming words addressed to <s>Rādhikā</s> by the enemy of <s>Mura</s> —
victorious is this [song] adorned by the poetry of <s>Jayadeva</s>, causing the pride of proud women to be cut asunder! || GG_10.9 ||
NOTE:
{"jayati" (is victorious) is an alternate reading.}
NOTE:

{"jayati padmāvatī-ramaṇa-jayadeva-kavi-bhāratī-bhaṇitam atiśātam" (Victorious is this most sharp [song] spoken by the poetry of the poet <s>Jayadeva</s>, beloved of <s>Padmāvatī</s>) is an alternate reading preserved in the commentary.}

children.text: parihara kṛtātaṅke śaṅkāṃ tvayā satataṃ ghana-stana-jaghanayākrānte svānte parānavakāśinī |
children.translated_text: Abandon suspicion, O fearful one! In your heart, occupied by heavy breasts and hips, no other enters — there is no space for another. No other fortunate one enters my inner being, O beloved;

children.text: viśati vitanor anyo dhanyo na ko'pi mamāntaraṃ praṇayini parīrambhārambhe vidhehi vidheyatām || GG_10.10 ||
children.translated_text: at the commencement of our embrace, O loving one, submit with compliance! || GG_10.10 ||
O innocent one, inflict upon me merciless tooth-bites, tight arm-vine embraces, and firm breast-pressing!

children.text: caṇḍi tvam eva mudam udvaha pañca-bāṇa-cāṇḍāla-kāṇḍa-dalanād asavaḥ prayāntu || GG_10.11 ||
children.translated_text: O fierce one, you alone bear the joy — [even] if life departs from the assault of the five-arrowed outcaste [<s>Kāma</s>]'s shafts! || GG_10.11 ||
NOTE:
{"prayānti" (they depart) [variant reading]}
O moon-faced one, your curved eyebrow shines — a terrifying serpent of time, causing delusion in young men;
for dispelling the fear born of that [serpent], the nectar of your lips is indeed the perfect mantra for the young! || GG_10.12 ||

children.text: vyathayati vṛthā maunaṃ tanvi prapañcaya pañcamaṃ taruṇi madhurālāpais tāpaṃ vinodaya dṛṣṭibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Silence distresses in vain, O slender one — elaborate the fifth [note of love]; O youthful one, dispel the burning with sweet conversations and with glances!

children.text: sumukhi vimukhī-bhāvaṃ tāvad vimuñca na muñca māṃ svayam atiśaya-snigdho mugdhe priyo'yam upasthitaḥ || GG_10.13 ||
children.translated_text: O beautiful-faced one, abandon your aversion for now — do not release me; this beloved of yours, exceedingly tender, O innocent one, has come before you! || GG_10.13 ||

children.text: bandhūka-dyuti-bāndhavo'yam adharaḥ snigdho madhūka-cchavir gaṇḍaś caṇḍi cakāsti nīla-nalina-śrī-mocanaṃ locanam |
children.translated_text: This lip, companion of the <s>Bandhūka</s> flower's radiance; this cheek, tender as the glow of the <s>Madhūka</s>; O fierce one, the eye shines, liberating the beauty of the blue lotus;

children.text: nāsābhyeti tila-prasūna-padavīṃ kundābha-danti priye prāyas tvan-mukha-sevayā vijayate viśvaṃ sa puṣpāyudhaḥ || GG_10.14 ||
children.translated_text: the nose follows the path of the sesame blossom; O beloved with teeth like <s>Kunda</s> (jasmine) — it seems that through the service of your face, the flower-weaponed one [<s>Kāma</s>] conquers the entire world! || GG_10.14 ||
NOTE:
{"senayeti" (with the army) is an alternate reading preserved in the commentary.}

body.text: dṛśau tava madālase vadanam indu-sandīpanaṃ gatir jana-manoramā vijita-rambhaṃ ūru-dvayam |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"vidhuta-" (shaken) is the reading in <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition.}

children.text: ratis tava kalāvatī rucira-citra-lekhe bhruvāv aho vibudha-yauvataṃ vahasi tanvi pṛthvī-gatā || GG_10.15 ||
children.translated_text: your love-play is full of art, your eyebrows are beautiful painted lines — ah, O slender one, you bear upon the earth the youthfulness of the gods! || GG_10.15 ||

body.translated_text: Your eyes are languid with love, your face kindles like the moon, your gait charms the minds of people, your pair of thighs surpasses [those of] <s>Rambhā</s>;

body.text: sa prītiṃ tanutāṃ hariḥ kuvalayāpīḍena sārdhaṃ raṇe rādhā-pīna-payodhara-smaraṇa-kṛt-kumbhena sambhedavān |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"prītiṃ vas tanutāṃ" (may he extend joy to you) is the reading in <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition.}

children.text: yatra svidyati mīlati kṣaṇam api kṣipraṃ tad-ālokana-vyāmohena jitaṃ jitaṃ jitam abhūt kaṃsasya kolāhalaḥ || GG_10.16 ||
children.translated_text: where he perspired and closed his eyes for an instant, and swiftly through the bewilderment of beholding [them], there arose the triumphant cry 'Conquered! Conquered! Conquered!' — the uproar against <s>Kaṃsa</s>! || GG_10.16 ||

body.translated_text: May that <s>Hari</s> increase [our] joy — he who, together with [the demon] <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> in battle, whose frontal globe recalled <s>Rādhā</s>'s full breasts, clashing together,

children.translated_text: NOTE:

children.text: {yatra svidyati mīlati kṣaṇam atha kṣipte dvipe tat-kṣaṇāt kaṃsasyālam abhūj jitaṃ jitaṃ jitam iti vyāmoha-kolāhalaḥ || iti haridāsa-saṃskaraṇa-pāṭhaḥ.}
children.translated_text: {"yatra svidyati mīlati kṣaṇam atha kṣipte dvipe tat-kṣaṇāt kaṃsasyālam abhūj jitaṃ jitaṃ jitam iti vyāmoha-kolāhalaḥ" (Where he perspired and closed his eyes for a moment, and then when the elephant was hurled, at that instant there arose for <s>Kaṃsa</s> the bewildered uproar: 'Conquered! Conquered! Conquered!') is the reading in <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition.}
NOTE:
{"sāmoda-" (fragrant) is found in some [manuscripts]; "sānanda-govinda" (the joyful <s>Govinda</s>) is the reading in <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition.}

body.translated_text:
Eleventh Canto
<s>Sānanda-Dāmodara</s> (The Joyful <s>Dāmodara</s>)

children.text: suciram anunayena prīṇayitvā mṛgākṣīṃ gatavati kṛtaveśe keśave kuñja-śayyām |
children.translated_text: Having long pleased the deer-eyed one with tender entreaties, when <s>Keśava</s> had gone to the bower-bed, adorned and dressed,

children.text: racita-rucira-bhūṣāṃ dṛṣṭi-moṣe pradoṣe sphurati niravasādāṃ kāpi rādhāṃ jagāda || GG_11.1 ||
children.translated_text: in the dusk that steals the sight, radiant and free from dejection, a certain [friend] spoke to <s>Rādhā</s>. || GG_11.1 ||

body.translated_text: || Song 20 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Vasanta</s> rāga and <s>Yati</s> tāla.
He who has composed flattering words at [your] feet, who has performed prostrations [at them],
has now gone to the lovely bower of <s>Vañjula</s> (Asoka) trees, to the bed of love. || GG_11.2 ||

body.translated_text: O innocent one, follow <s>Madhu</s>'s slayer (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) who has gone ahead — follow him, O <s>Rādhikā</s>! || Refrain ||

children.translated_text: With heavy hips and the weight of [her] breasts, her gait slightly slow in her movement,
with anklets of jingling gems — approach him, assume the gait of a swan! [GG 11.3]
NOTE:
{"nikāram" [is a variant reading].}
NOTE:
{"ramaṇī-" [variant]}
NOTE:
{"madhuripu-rāvam" (the call of the foe of <s>Madhu</s>) [variant]}
embrace the spirit of the flocks of cuckoos, who celebrate the rule of the flower-bowed one (<s>Kāma</s>). [GG 11.4]

body.translated_text: Listen to the ever more delightful humming of the bees, enchanting the young women,

children.translated_text: With clusters of tender shoots swaying in the wind, like hands, the creeper-thickets

children.text: preraṇam iva karabhoru karoti gatiṃ prati muñca vilambam || GG_11.5 ||
children.translated_text: as if urging you onward, O beautiful-thighed one — abandon delay in your going! [GG 11.5]
Trembling as if under the waves of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Love-god), hinting at <s>Hari</s>'s embrace,
ask these pitcher-like breasts, bearing a necklace of pure water-drops! [GG 11.6]

children.text: adhigatam akhila-sakhībhir idaṃ tava vapur api rati-raṇa-sajjam |
children.translated_text: All your companions have noticed that your body too is ready for the battle of love —

children.text: caṇḍi rasita-raśanā-rava-ḍiṇḍimam abhisara sarasam alajjam || GG_11.7 ||
children.translated_text: O passionate one, with the sound of your girdle-bells as your war-drum, go forth to the tryst boldly and without shame! [GG 11.7]
Resting your hand playfully on your companion's shoulder, with nails lovely as <s>Kāma</s>'s arrows,

children.text: cala valaya-kvaṇitair avabodhaya harim api nija-gati-śīlaṃ || GG_11.8 ||
children.translated_text: go forth — and with the tinkling of your bracelets, awaken even <s>Hari</s> to the manner of your approach! [GG 11.8]
NOTE:
{"nigadita" [is a variant reading].}
This [song] spoken by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>, having surpassed [all other] necklaces, having set aside coyness,
may it rest unceasingly upon the throats of those whose minds are fixed on <s>Hari</s>! [GG 11.9]

body.text: sā māṃ drakṣyati vakṣyati smara-kathāṃ praty-aṅgam āliṅganaiḥ prītiṃ yāsyati raṃsyate sakhi samāgatyeti cintākulaḥ |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"sañcintayan" is <s>Haridāsa</s>'s reading.}

children.text: sa tvāṃ paśyati vepate pulakayaty ānandati svidyati pratyudgacchati mūrcchati sthira-tamah-puñje nikuñje prīyaḥ || GG_11.10 ||
children.translated_text: he sees you, trembles, bristles with goosebumps, rejoices, perspires, comes forward to meet you, and swoons — [your] beloved, in the bower dense with darkness. [GG 11.10]

body.translated_text: "She will see me, she will speak of love, she will delight in embraces limb by limb, she will make love" — thus thinking anxiously, O friend, upon her coming,

children.text: akṣṇor nikṣipad añjanaṃ śravaṇayos tāpiñcha-gucchāvalīṃ mūrdhni śyāma-saroja-dāma kucayoḥ kastūrikā-patrakam |
children.translated_text: She placed collyrium on her eyes, clusters of <s>tāpiñcha</s> [flowers] on her ears, a garland of dark lotuses on her head, a musk-leaf pattern upon her breasts —

children.text: dhūrtānām abhisāra-sambhrama-jūṣāṃ viṣvaṅ-nikuñje sakhi dhvāntaṃ nīla-nicola-cāru sudṛśāṃ praty-aṅgam aliṅgati || GG_11.11 ||
children.translated_text: O friend, for the bold women hastening to their trysts, the darkness, dark-blue like a beautiful dark garment, embraces every limb in the spreading bower. [GG 11.11]
NOTE:
{"abhisāra-satvara-hṛdāṃ" (of those whose hearts hasten to the tryst) is the reading of <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition.}
For the women going to their trysts, whose bodies are fair as saffron, with lines [of decoration] tied all around by clusters of radiance,

children.text: etat tamāla-dala-nīlatamaṃ tamisraṃ tat-prema-hema-nikaṣopalatāṃ tanoti || GG_11.12 ||
children.translated_text: this darkness, dark as a <s>tamāla</s> leaf, extends like a touchstone of gold for testing their love. [GG 11.12]
NOTE:
{"mañjīra" (anklets) is <s>Haridāsa</s>'s reading.}

children.text: dvāre nikuñja-nilayasya hariṃ nirīkṣya vrīḍāvatīm atha sakhīṃ īyam ity uvaca || GG_11.13 ||
children.translated_text: she, bashful, spoke thus to her companion: [GG 11.13]

body.translated_text: Seeing <s>Hari</s> at the door of the bower-dwelling, illuminated by the radiance of jeweled necklaces, golden girdle-cords, armlets, bangles, and gems,
|| Composition 21 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Varāḍī</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Rūpaka</s> <s>tāla</s>
In the lovely bower-floor, a pleasure-house for love-play,
radiant with a face laughing in the rapture of love — [GG 11.14]

body.translated_text: Enter, O <s>Rādhā</s>, into the presence of <s>Mādhava</s> here! [refrain]

children.translated_text: NOTE:

children.text: {haridāsasya saṃskaraṇe, ḥpraviśa rādheḥ ity-ādi dhruva-padaṃ pratiślokasya prathama-dvitīya-caraṇayor madhye gīyate.}
children.translated_text: {In <s>Haridāsa</s>'s edition, the refrain "praviśa rādhe" etc. is sung between the first and second lines of each verse.}
NOTE:
{"bhavad-" is
an
alternate reading.}
radiant with a swaying necklace upon your pitcher-like breasts — [GG 11.15]

body.translated_text: On the excellent bed of fresh, gleaming <s>aśoka</s> leaves,

children.translated_text: In the chamber fragrant with a heap of flowers,
radiant with a body tender as flowers — [GG 11.16]
NOTE:
{"mṛdu-cala-malaya-" is <s>Haridāsa</s>'s alternate reading.}
radiant though frightened by the multitude of <s>Madana</s>'s (the Love-god's) arrows — [GG 11.17]

body.translated_text: In the gentle, moving <s>Malaya</s> breeze, fragrant and cool,

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"kusuma-śara" (flower-arrowed) or "madana-rasa" (love's essence) are
alternate
readings.}
NOTE:
{"vilasa rati-valita-lalita-gīte" (radiant with graceful songs turned by love) is <s>Haridāsa</s>'s reading. In that reading,
"rasa"
-valita- is also [found].}
In the dense thicket of spreading vines with fresh leaves,
radiant with languid, full hips — [GG 11.18]
In the humming of bees delighted by honey,
radiant with the passionate spirit of love's essence — [GG 11.19]
NOTE:
{"rabhasa-rasa-" is <s>Haridāsa</s>'s reading.}
In [the grove] resonant with the sweeter calls of flocks of cuckoos,
radiant with the beauty of gleaming teeth — [GG 11.20]
Having arranged a joyful assembly for <s>Padmāvatī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
grant hundreds of auspicious blessings, O <s>Murāri</s>!
So speaks <s>Jayadeva</s>, king among poet-kings. [GG 11.21]

children.text: tvāṃ cittena ciraṃ vahann ayam atiśrānto bhṛśaṃ tāpitaḥ kandarpeṇa ca pātum icchati sudhā-sambādha-bimbādharam |
children.translated_text: Having borne you in his heart for so long, this one is utterly exhausted, grievously scorched by <s>Kandarpa</s> (the Love-god), and longs to drink the nectar of your <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips —

children.text: asyāṅkaṃ tad alaṅkuru kṣaṇam iha bhrū-kṣepa-lakṣmī-lava-krīte dāsa ivopasevita-padāmbhoje kutaḥ sambhramaḥ || GG_11.22 ||
children.translated_text: so adorn his lap for a moment here; he is like a slave bought for a mere fraction of the beauty of your brow's glance, attending at your lotus feet — why this apprehension? [GG 11.22]
She, with trembling, joyful eyes fixed on <s>Govinda</s>,
her lovely anklets jingling, entered the dwelling. [GG 11.23]
NOTE:
{"praviveśābhiveśanam" is <s>Haridāsa</s>'s reading.}

body.translated_text: || Composition 22 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Varāḍī</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Yati</s> <s>tāla</s>
Blossoming with various transformations of emotion at the sight of <s>Rādhā</s>'s face,
like the ocean with towering waves made restless by the sight of the moon's orb — [GG 11.24]
<s>Hari</s>, of single passion, whose long-desired play [was now fulfilled],
she beheld him — his face submissive to great joy, the abode of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Love-god). [refrain]

body.text: hāram amalatara-tāram urasi dadhataṃ parilambya vidūram |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"parirabhya" (embracing) is
an
alternate reading.}
like the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s> mingled with clusters of bright foam — [GG 11.25]

body.translated_text: Wearing on his chest a necklace of purest pearls, hanging far down,

children.translated_text: His dark, soft, rounded body wrapped in a pale garment,
like a blue lotus with its base encircled by a mass of yellow pollen — [GG 11.26]
His enchanting face, generating the passion of love with the movement of restless, glancing eyes,
like a pond in autumn with a pair of <s>khañjana</s> (wagtail) birds playing in the expanse of a blooming lotus — [GG 11.27]
The beauty of his earrings, like the sun, meeting [his] lotus-face upon close inspection,
arousing desire for love with his lip-petals, beautiful with the radiance of a smile — [GG 11.28]
His beautiful flower-bedecked hair, like a charming cloud-mass sprinkled with moonbeams,
with a pure sandal-paste <s>tilaka</s> set upon [his brow] like a spotless moon-orb risen in the darkness — [GG 11.29]
His body bristling all over with the abundance of goosebumps, unsteady with the arts of love-play,
his handsome form resplendent with the radiance of clusters of jeweled ornaments — [GG 11.30]
This [song] spoken by <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s>, whose ornamental glory is doubled,

children.text: praṇamata hṛdi vinidhāya hariṃ suciraṃ sukṛtodaya-sāram || GG_11.31 ||
children.translated_text: bow down, placing <s>Hari</s> in your heart for a long time — the essence of the arising of good merit! [GG 11.31]
NOTE:
{"patitayoḥ" (having fallen) is <s>Haridāsa Dāsa</s>'s reading.}

children.text: idānīṃ rādhāyāḥ priyatama-samāloka-samaye papāta svedāmbu-prasara iva harṣāśru-nikaraḥ || GG_11.32 ||
children.translated_text: now, at the moment of <s>Rādhā</s>'s beholding her dearest beloved, there fell a flood of tears of joy, like a rush of perspiration. [GG 11.32]

body.translated_text: Crossing beyond the corner of her eyes, as if with the effort of traveling the path to the ears, the most restless pupils of her eyes having moved,

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{"samāyāta-" is
an
alternate reading.}

children.text: bhajantyās talpāntaṃ kṛta-kapaṭa-kaṇḍūti-pihita-smitaṃ yāte gehād bahir avahitālī-parijane |
children.translated_text: As she approached the edge of the couch, with her smile concealed by a feigned itch, when [her companions] had gone outside the house with their attendants carefully dismissed,

children.text: priyāsyaṃ paśyantyāḥ smara-paravaśākūta-subhagaṃ salajjā lajjāpi vyagamad iva dūraṃ mṛga-dṛśaḥ || GG_11.33 ||
children.translated_text: as the doe-eyed one gazed upon the face of her beloved, beautiful with the signs of desire overcome by love — even her modesty itself seemed to flee far away. [GG 11.33]

body.text: sānandaṃ nanda-sūnur diśatu mitaparaṃ saṃmadaṃ manda-mandaṃ rādhām ādhāya bāhvor vivaram anu drḍhaṃ pīḍayan prīti-yogāt |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{This verse does not appear in <s>Haridāsa Dāsa</s>'s edition.}

children.text: tuṅgau tasyā urojāv atanu-varatanor nirgatau mā sma bhūtāṃ pṛṣṭhaṃ nirbhidya tasmād bahir iti valita-grīvam ālokayan vaḥ || GG_11.34 ||
children.translated_text: her high breasts, pressed against his broad, slender body — "may they not come out through the back!" — craning his neck to look [at her in concern], may he [protect] you! [GG 11.34]

body.translated_text: May the son of <s>Nanda</s>, having placed <s>Rādhā</s> in his arms and pressing her tightly with love, grant you boundless, supreme delight, gently, gently —

children.text: jaya-śrī-vinyastair mahita iva mandāra-kusumaiḥ svayaṃ sindūreṇa dvipa-raṇa-mudā mudrita iva |
children.translated_text: As if honored by <s>mandāra</s> flowers placed by the goddess of victory, as if stamped in delight from an elephant-battle's own vermillion,

children.text: bhujāpīḍa-krīḍā-hata-kuvalayāpīḍa-kariṇaḥ prakīrṇāsṛg-bindur jayati bhuja-daṇḍo murajitaḥ || GG_11.35 ||
children.translated_text: the mighty arm of the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, who crushed the elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s> in the sport of arm-wrestling, scattered with drops of blood — it triumphs! [GG 11.35]

body.text: saundaryaika-nidher anaṅga-lalanā-lāvaṇya-līlā-juṣo rādhāyā hṛdi palvale manasija-krīḍaika-raṅga-sthale |

children.translated_text: NOTE:
{This verse does not appear in <s>Haridāsa Dāsa</s>'s edition.}

children.text: ramyoroja-saroja-khelana-rasitvād ātmanaḥ khyāpayan dhyātur mānasa-rāja-haṃsa-nibhatāṃ deyān mukundo mudam || GG_11.36 ||
children.translated_text: proclaiming himself delighted in the play of the lovely lotus-breasts, may <s>Mukunda</s> grant the joy of being like a royal swan in the mind of the one who meditates [on him]! [GG 11.36]

body.translated_text: In the pool of <s>Rādhā</s>'s heart — sole treasury of beauty, graced with the charm and play of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (the Love-god's) beloved —the sole arena of the Love-god's sport,
Twelfth Canto: <s>Suprīta-Pītāmbara</s> (The Well-Pleased Wearer of Yellow Robes)

children.translated_text: When the company of friends had departed, her lip bathed in a smile swelling with desire barely hidden behind a deep mass of modesty,

children.text: sarasa-manasaṃ dṛṣṭvā rādhāṃ muhur nava-pallava-prasava-śayane nikṣiptākṣīm uvāca hariḥ priyām || GG_12.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, seeing <s>Rādhā</s>, her mind full of passion, her eyes cast down upon the bed of fresh blossoms and shoots, spoke to his beloved: [GG 12.1]

body.translated_text: || Composition 23 ||

children.translated_text: Sung in <s>Vibhāsa</s> <s>rāga</s> with <s>Ekatālī</s> <s>tāla</s>
On the bed of tender shoots, O lovely one, place your lotus feet;

children.text: tava pada-pallava-vairi-parābhavam idam anubhavatu suveśaṃ || GG_12.2 ||
children.translated_text: let this beautiful [bed] experience the defeat of the enemy of your foot-petals. [GG 12.2]

body.text: kṣaṇam adhunā nārāyaṇam anugatam anusara rādhike || dhruva ||
body.translated_text: For a moment now, follow <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> who has come to you — come, O <s>Rādhikā</s>! [refrain]

children.text: kara-kamalena karomi caraṇam aham āgamitāsi vidūram |
children.translated_text: With my lotus-hands I shall tend your feet — you have come from afar;

children.text: kṣaṇam upakuru śayanopari mām iva nūpuram anugati-śūram || GG_12.3 ||
children.translated_text: rest upon the bed a moment — upon me, like an anklet, faithful in following your steps! [GG 12.3]

children.text: vadana-sudhā-nidhi-galitam amṛtam iva racaya vacanam anukūlam |
children.translated_text: Let fall from the nectar-ocean of your face words favorable, like flowing ambrosia;

children.text: viraham ivāpanayāmi payodhara-rodhakam urasi dukūlaṃ || GG_12.4 ||
children.translated_text: as if removing separation, I remove the cloth that obstructs your breasts from my chest! [GG 12.4]
Your pitcher-like breasts, bristling [with goosebumps] as if trembling with the eagerness of a lover's embrace, so rarely attained —
